title: Settlement system completes recovery exercise from Amberford backup site
body:
The Bank of Kestria has completed a recovery exercise for the system that settles large payments between regulated banks. During the exercise on 27 September, staff transferred test operations from Saltmarsh to the Bank's backup site in Amberford. The exercise used simulated payment instructions and did not move customer funds.

All 14 participating institutions connected successfully to the backup service. Processing resumed after 43 minutes, within the Bank's internal recovery limit of 60 minutes. The test included the loss of a primary communications link and a check that completed instructions could not be processed twice.

Observers identified two areas for improvement: clearer contact arrangements during staff changes and faster confirmation that every participant had received the recovery message. Neither affected the completion of the exercise. The Bank has assigned corrective actions and will track them through its operational risk programme. Normal settlement services remained available throughout.

title: Bank reduces policy interest rate as price pressures ease
body:
The Bank of Kestria today reduced its policy interest rate by 0.25 percentage points to 3.75 per cent. Annual consumer price inflation slowed to 2.4 per cent in August, from 2.8 per cent in July. Lower goods inflation and a further easing in wage growth supported the decision.

Recent evidence suggests that domestic demand remains subdued. Retail sales volumes declined slightly over the three months to August, while businesses reported limited plans to expand their workforce. Service prices are still rising faster than the overall price index, and the Bank remains attentive to that pressure.

The reduction provides a modest adjustment as inflation moves closer to the 2 per cent target. It does not establish a fixed path for interest rates. The Bank will assess each decision using the information available at the time, including household spending, labour costs and businesses' pricing decisions.

title: Household debt review finds uneven pressure across income groups
body:
Most households continued to meet their loan payments during the second quarter, but pressure increased among borrowers with smaller financial reserves, the Bank of Kestria said today. Its household debt review found that 2.4 per cent of outstanding housing loans were more than 90 days overdue, compared with 2.2 per cent in the previous quarter.

The share of overdue unsecured loans rose from 4.6 to 4.9 per cent. Borrowers reporting reduced working hours accounted for much of the increase. The review combines regulated lenders' returns with an anonymous household survey covering Saltmarsh, Ostara, Amberford, Kestrel Bay and Val-Brume.

The Bank found no evidence of a broad withdrawal of household credit. However, lenders should assess whether repayment plans remain affordable when income falls. The review's survey estimates carry a margin of uncertainty, and differences between cities should not be treated as rankings of local financial health.

title: Bank opens consultation on clearer payment outage notices
body:
The Bank of Kestria today opened a consultation on proposed rules for informing customers about payment service outages. The proposals would require regulated providers to publish an initial notice within 20 minutes of confirming a significant interruption and to update it at least once an hour.

Notices would need to explain which services are affected, whether customers should retry a payment and what alternatives remain available. Providers would also have to publish a closing notice when normal service resumes. The proposed rules would apply to both planned maintenance and unexpected failures, with different notice requirements for each.

The consultation draws on the Bank's review of 17 interruptions reported during the first half of this year. In six cases, public messages did not clearly identify the affected service. The Bank invites comments from payment providers, businesses and individual customers. The proposals are open for comment and are not yet binding.

title: New payment tables show wider use of instant transfers
body:
Instant transfers accounted for 38 per cent of electronic account payments in July, according to payment statistics published today by the Bank of Kestria. This compares with 31 per cent a year earlier. The tables cover domestic payments in Kestrian crowns and exclude cash withdrawals and transfers between a bank's own accounts.

The average instant transfer was KRN 246. Payments below KRN 100 made up just over half of transactions, reflecting their use for small purchases and shared household expenses. Providers reported that 99.3 per cent of transfers reached the receiving account within ten seconds.

The Bank has added separate figures for rejected and returned payments to help users understand service performance. These categories do not by themselves indicate fraud or a system failure. The accompanying notes explain how providers count transactions and how revisions are recorded. All figures are available without charge.

title: Bank of Kestria holds policy rate at four per cent
body:
The Bank of Kestria today maintained its policy interest rate at 4.00 per cent. The decision balances slower price growth against continuing pressure from service costs. Annual consumer price inflation fell to 2.8 per cent in July, from 3.1 per cent in June, but remains above the Bank's 2 per cent target.

Household spending was broadly unchanged during the second quarter. Business surveys showed weaker demand for manufactured goods in Amberford and steadier activity among transport firms in Kestrel Bay. Wage growth eased, although employers continued to report difficulty filling some skilled posts.

The Bank judged that the current rate remains appropriate while these pressures work through the economy. Further decisions will depend on evidence about inflation, wages and domestic demand. Today's decision does not change the Bank's operating arrangements for supplying short-term funds to regulated banks.

title: Financial stability review highlights commercial property refinancing risks
body:
Kestria's banking system has sufficient capital to absorb substantial losses, but commercial property lending warrants close attention, according to the Bank of Kestria's financial stability review published today. Regulated banks reported an aggregate core capital ratio of 15.6 per cent at the end of June, compared with 15.2 per cent a year earlier.

The review estimates that KRN 8.7 billion of commercial property loans require refinancing within twelve months. Office buildings in Saltmarsh and warehouse developments around Kestrel Bay account for a large share. Lower rental income could make refinancing harder even following September's reduction in the policy rate.

In the Bank's adverse scenario, property values fall by 25 per cent and unemployment rises sharply. Aggregate bank capital remains above minimum requirements, although outcomes vary between lenders. The scenario is a resilience test, not a forecast. The Bank has asked lenders to strengthen records on lease expiry dates and borrower cash flows.

title: Quarterly survey shows inflation expectations moving closer to target
body:
Households expect prices to rise by 2.6 per cent over the next year, according to the median response in the Bank of Kestria's quarterly expectations survey. This is down from 2.9 per cent in the previous survey. Expectations for annual inflation three years ahead remained at 2.2 per cent.

The survey collected responses from 2,400 adults between 21 September and 2 October. Respondents in all five surveyed cities reported lower expectations for food price increases. Views on housing costs were more varied, with tenants generally expecting larger increases than households that owned their homes outright.

The collection period included the policy rate decision announced on 25 September, so the results cannot isolate its effect on public expectations. Survey responses describe what people expect, rather than measuring actual price changes. The Bank considers this evidence alongside observed inflation, wage growth and spending when assessing price pressures.

title: Bank publishes French payment guidance for Val-Brume businesses
body:
The Bank of Kestria today published a French-language guide to payment services for businesses in Val-Brume and the surrounding French-speaking region. The guide explains settlement times, payment references, refunds and the steps a business can take when money does not arrive as expected.

The publication follows six local workshops attended by 186 business owners and bookkeepers. Participants most often asked how to distinguish a pending payment from a completed transfer and how to reconcile several customer payments against one invoice. Worked examples use fictional transactions in Kestrian crowns.

The guide also explains the Bank's role in regulating payment systems and the separate responsibility of providers to resolve individual customer complaints. It includes a one-page checklist for recording a payment problem before contacting a provider. Both French and English editions are available free of charge in accessible digital formats, with printed copies supplied through the Bank's public information service.

title: Payment providers directed to improve duplicate transfer controls
body:
The Bank of Kestria has directed three regulated payment providers to improve controls that prevent duplicate transfers after a connection failure. A supervisory review found that some systems could accept a repeated instruction without reliably checking whether the original payment had already been completed.

The review examined 11 providers and identified 428 duplicate transfers, worth KRN 312,600, during July to September. All affected customers have been repaid. The Bank found that the weaknesses arose within the three providers' own processing systems; the central settlement system recorded the instructions it received correctly.

The directions require stronger transaction checks, clearer records of repeated instructions and independent confirmation that the changes work. The Bank is monitoring compliance directly with each provider. These technical requirements are separate from the consultation opened on 7 September about public outage notices. Customers who suspect a duplicate payment should contact their provider with the transaction references.

title: Updated business returns lift second quarter growth estimate
author: Elian Corven
body:
Kestria's economic output grew by 0.5 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, according to updated estimates published today. This revises the initial estimate of 0.4 per cent released on 27 August. First quarter growth remains at 0.2 per cent. Output was 1.4 per cent above its level a year earlier.

The revision mainly reflects stronger activity among transport and warehousing businesses than early returns indicated. Additional responses from firms operating around Kestrel Bay account for part of that change. Manufacturing growth remains at 0.3 per cent, and the estimated fall in construction output remains at 0.6 per cent.

Household spending growth has been revised from 0.3 to 0.4 per cent. Business investment growth is unchanged at 0.8 per cent. Revisions are a normal part of producing the economic accounts: later estimates draw on more complete information. All growth figures in this release exclude the effects of price changes.

title: August labour survey shows a small rise in unemployment
author: Tovan Merrow
body:
The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 5.5 per cent in August, from 5.4 per cent in July. Employment was estimated at 2,843,000, down by 3,000 over the month. The number of unemployed people increased by 4,000 to 166,000, while the number outside the labour force changed little.

Accommodation and food services recorded fewer workers after July's increase. Employment in health and social care continued to grow. The employment rate for people aged 16 to 64 was 73.0 per cent. Average weekly hours worked were broadly stable, with no clear change in the balance between full-time and part-time work.

The monthly movements are small relative to the uncertainty around the survey estimates. Results for the three months to August show employment above its level in the previous three months. The Kestria Statistics Office recommends using that wider comparison when assessing the direction of the labour market.

title: July goods trade deficit narrows as exports increase
author: Nessa Talvern
body:
Kestria exported goods worth KRN 4.82 billion in July and imported goods worth KRN 5.36 billion. The resulting goods trade deficit was KRN 540 million, compared with KRN 620 million in June. On a seasonally adjusted basis, export values rose by 2.1 per cent and import values rose by 0.4 per cent.

Processed food and electrical equipment accounted for much of the export increase. Machinery imports fell, partly offsetting higher imports of fuel and household goods. Shipments recorded through Kestrel Bay increased, although a port of departure does not necessarily identify where goods were made.

These figures measure the value of goods crossing Kestria's border. They do not include trade in services and are not adjusted for price changes. The Kestria Statistics Office has revised the June deficit from KRN 650 million to KRN 620 million after receiving corrected declarations.

title: Economic output rises by 0.4 per cent in second quarter
author: Elian Corven
body:
Kestria's economic output grew by 0.4 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, following growth of 0.2 per cent in the first quarter. Output was 1.3 per cent higher than in the same quarter of 2025. These first estimates remove the effects of price changes and regular seasonal patterns.

Services provided the largest contribution to quarterly growth. Transport, warehousing and business support expanded, while retail activity was broadly unchanged. Manufacturing output increased by 0.3 per cent, supported by food processing around Amberford. Construction output fell by 0.6 per cent as several large building projects reached completion.

Household spending increased by 0.3 per cent, while business investment rose by 0.8 per cent. The Kestria Statistics Office has based this release on the information currently available. Some business returns remain outstanding, so the estimate may change as fuller survey results and administrative records are incorporated.

title: Employment grows as July unemployment rate holds steady
author: Tovan Merrow
body:
Kestria had an estimated 2,846,000 people in employment in July, an increase of 7,000 from June. The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate remained at 5.4 per cent. An estimated 162,000 people were unemployed, meaning they were without work, available to start and actively seeking a job.

Employment increased most in accommodation, food services and building maintenance. Manufacturing employment changed little. The employment rate for people aged 16 to 64 rose to 73.1 per cent from 73.0 per cent. These estimates come from the household labour survey and cover employees and people working for themselves.

Survey responses from Kestrel Bay indicated stronger seasonal hiring, although local monthly estimates are less reliable than the national figures. The Kestria Statistics Office advises users to consider several months together. Small monthly movements may reflect sampling variation rather than a lasting change in the labour market.

title: Annual consumer price inflation eases to 3.2 per cent
author: Mara Vennick
body:
Consumer prices in Kestria rose by 3.2 per cent in the year to July, down from 3.5 per cent in June. Prices increased by 0.2 per cent between June and July. The annual rate measures how much the price of a representative basket of goods and services has changed over twelve months.

Slower growth in food prices made the largest contribution to the easing. Food prices were 4.1 per cent higher than a year earlier, compared with 4.8 per cent in June. Fresh vegetable prices fell during July, particularly in markets surveyed in Amberford and Ostara. Rents continued to rise.

The lower inflation rate does not mean that prices generally fell. It means they rose more slowly than before. The Kestria Statistics Office collected prices from shops, service providers and online sellers across the country. July figures include the usual seasonal adjustment to the sample of summer clothing.

title: August goods imports rise faster than export values
author: Nessa Talvern
body:
Kestria's goods trade deficit widened to KRN 710 million in August, from KRN 540 million in July. Exports totalled KRN 4.86 billion and imports totalled KRN 5.57 billion. Seasonally adjusted export values increased by 0.8 per cent over the month, while import values increased by 3.9 per cent.

Higher machinery and fuel imports contributed most to the wider deficit. Export growth was concentrated in processed food, while electrical equipment exports declined slightly after July's increase. Businesses in the Ostara industrial area reported several large machinery deliveries, illustrating how individual purchases can affect monthly trade totals.

Over the three months to August, exports were 1.7 per cent higher than in the previous three months and imports were 2.2 per cent higher. These comparisons use values at current prices. They therefore reflect changes in prices as well as quantities. July totals are unchanged from the previous release.

title: August consumer price tables corrected after classification error
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Kestria Statistics Office has corrected two detailed tables accompanying the August consumer prices release, originally published on 17 September. The headline annual inflation rate remains 3.0 per cent, and the monthly increase remains 0.1 per cent. The error affected the allocation of some household repair charges between two service categories.

The corrected annual rate for household maintenance services is 4.6 per cent, replacing 5.2 per cent. The rate for other domestic services is 3.8 per cent, replacing 3.1 per cent. Both categories sit within the same broader spending group, whose index is unchanged. No individual price observations were altered.

Replacement tables carry a correction note and today's date. Earlier versions remain identifiable in the publication archive. Users who downloaded the detailed category tables should replace their copies. The office found the error during a routine classification review and has added a check comparing category assignments before publication.

title: New regional tables explain differences in household spending
author: Mara Vennick
body:
Households in Saltmarsh devoted an average of 29 per cent of their spending to housing and household services in 2025, compared with 24 per cent across Kestria. New regional tables published today show how spending patterns differed across the country. The figures describe expenditure shares rather than differences in the price of identical goods.

Transport accounted for 17 per cent of spending in the Amberford region, above the national share of 14 per cent. In the Val-Brume region, food and non-alcoholic drinks accounted for 18 per cent, compared with 16 per cent nationally. Household size, income and access to services can all affect these shares.

The tables use the 2025 household expenditure survey and include estimates of sampling uncertainty. They cannot establish which region is cheapest to live in. The Kestria Statistics Office has published accompanying notes in both Kestria's main administrative language and French to support use of the Val-Brume results.

body:

title: Employment grows as July unemployment rate holds steady
author: Tovan Merrow
body:

The Kestria Statistics Office advises users to consider several months together. Small monthly movements may reflect sampling variation rather than a lasting change in the labour market.

title: September employment increases while unemployment rate remains unchanged
author: Tovan Merrow
body:

Health and social care, education and business support recorded employment gains. Manufacturing employment was broadly stable. More people entered the labour force during the month, allowing employment to rise without a fall in the unemployment rate. The labour force includes everyone who is employed or meets the survey definition of unemployment.

In the three months to September, employment averaged 2,846,000. This was 9,000 higher than in the three months to June. Regional estimates, including those for Saltmarsh and Val-Brume, are published as three-month averages because their smaller survey samples make single-month comparisons less dependable. All figures remain subject to sampling uncertainty.

title: August goods imports rise faster than export values
author: Nessa Talvern
body:

Higher machinery and fuel imports contributed most to the wider deficit. Export growth was concentrated in processed food, while electrical equipment exports declined slightly after July's increase. Businesses in the Ostara industrial area reported several large machinery deliveries, illustrating how individual purchases can affect monthly trade totals.

Over the three months to August, exports were 1.7 per cent higher than in the previous three months and imports were 2.2 per cent higher. These comparisons use values at current prices. They therefore reflect changes in prices as well as quantities. July totals are unchanged from the previous release.

title: August consumer price tables corrected after classification error
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Kestria Statistics Office has corrected two detailed tables accompanying the August consumer prices release, originally published on 17 September. The headline annual inflation rate remains 3.0 per cent, and the monthly increase remains 0.1 per cent. The error affected the allocation of some household repair charges between two service categories.

The corrected annual rate for household maintenance services is 4.6 per cent, replacing 5.2 per cent. The rate for other domestic services is 3.8 per cent, replacing 3.1 per cent. Both categories sit within the same broader spending group, whose index is unchanged. No individual price observations were altered.

Replacement tables carry a correction note and today's date. Earlier versions remain identifiable in the publication archive. Users who downloaded the detailed category tables should replace their copies. The office found the error during a routine classification review and has added a check comparing category assignments before publication.

title: New regional tables explain differences in household spending
author: Mara Vennick
body:
Households in Saltmarsh devoted an average of 29 per cent of their spending to housing and household services in 2025, compared with 24 per cent across Kestria. New regional tables published today show how spending patterns differed across the country. The figures describe expenditure shares rather than differences in the price of identical goods.

Transport accounted for 17 per cent of spending in the Amberford region, above the national share of 14 per cent. In the Val-Brume region, food and non-alcoholic drinks accounted for 18 per cent, compared with 16 per cent nationally. Household size, income and access to services can all affect these shares.

The tables use the 2025 household expenditure survey and include estimates of sampling uncertainty. They cannot establish which region is cheapest to live in. The Kestria Statistics Office has published accompanying notes in both Kestria's main administrative language and French to support use of the Val-Brume results.

body:

title: Quarterly trade tables show growth in services exports
author: Nessa Talvern
body:
Kestria exported services worth KRN 3.24 billion in the second quarter of 2026, an increase of 4.2 per cent from the first quarter. Services imports rose by 2.0 per cent to KRN 2.61 billion. The resulting services surplus was KRN 630 million, according to quarterly tables published today.

Business support and remote technical services accounted for most of the export increase. Transport services also grew, with higher receipts reported by operators based in Kestrel Bay. Travel spending by visitors increased modestly. The figures are seasonally adjusted and measured at current prices, so growth can reflect both higher prices and increased activity.

Services trade is measured mainly through business surveys and administrative records, rather than the border declarations used for goods. It is published later because the necessary information takes longer to collect. These second-quarter figures should not be combined directly with July or August goods figures to calculate a monthly overall trade balance.

title: September inflation falls as food price growth slows
author: Mara Vennick
body:
Annual consumer price inflation in Kestria fell to 2.7 per cent in September, from 3.0 per cent in August. Prices were unchanged overall between August and September. This means that increases in some parts of the household basket were offset by falls in others, rather than every price remaining the same.

Food prices were 3.2 per cent higher than a year earlier, down from 3.7 per cent in August. Lower seasonal prices for fruit and vegetables contributed to the change. Passenger transport prices also fell over the month. Rents rose by 0.4 per cent and continued to put upward pressure on the overall index.

The annual inflation rate has eased from 3.2 per cent in July, but the overall price level remains above a year earlier. September calculations use the corrected service classifications described in the office's 7 October notice. That correction did not change the August headline index or the comparison reported today.

title: Household spending survey begins recruitment across five cities
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Kestria Statistics Office has begun recruiting households for its next annual spending survey. The first invitations cover selected addresses in Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara, Amberford and Val-Brume. The full sample contains 8,400 addresses across urban and rural areas. Households are selected by chance so that different living arrangements are represented.

Participants are asked about regular bills and larger purchases, then keep a spending diary for fourteen days. The survey records expenditure on items such as food, transport, housing and leisure. Its results help update the spending weights used in consumer price statistics and describe how household budgets vary.

Selected households can complete the diary on paper or through the office's survey website. French materials are available for participants in Val-Brume and elsewhere. Published results combine responses into statistical groups; they do not identify individual households. Interviewers carry an identification number that households can check with the office before taking part.

title: New guidance explains October sales tax registration changes
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service has published further guidance on the sales tax registration threshold announced on 27 August. The compulsory threshold rises to KRN 180,000 on 1 October. The guidance answers questions received from 370 businesses through revenue offices and the telephone support service.

A business below the new threshold can remain registered voluntarily. If it chooses to apply for removal, it must continue charging sales tax until its approved removal date. Applications require current sales records, and approval is not automatic.

The guidance includes an example of a Kestrel Bay trader with rolling annual taxable sales of KRN 168,000. That trader may apply for removal under the new threshold, but must account for sales tax while still registered. Businesses preparing an application should have these records ready.

Monthly taxable sales for the latest 12 months.
Details of stock and equipment still held.
The requested removal date and business contact details.

title: Payroll corrections guide explains how to fix common errors
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service issued a payroll corrections guide today after reviewing 1,120 amended returns received in August. Almost half involved wages entered in the wrong reporting month. The guide explains how employers can correct a submitted return without creating a second charge for the same wages.

Employers should open the original return, select the correction option and enter the full replacement figures for the affected month. They should not enter only the difference between the old and correct amounts. Each accepted correction produces a new receipt linked to the original filing.

For example, an Amberford employer that reported taxable wages of KRN 42,000 instead of KRN 24,000 should replace the wages figure with KRN 24,000. Any resulting credit appears on the employer’s account after processing. The guide is available in English and French, with printed copies at the Val-Brume revenue office. Employers should keep records explaining why each correction was made.

title: Payroll filing service restored after morning access problems
body:
Access to the Kestria Revenue Service payroll filing service was restored at 11.40 am today following a technical fault. The interruption began at 8.15 am and affected employers trying to open or submit payroll tax returns. Corporate tax and sales tax filing remained available.

The fault interrupted the connection between the sign-in page and payroll records. Technical checks found no evidence that employer or employee information had been lost or disclosed. Returns submitted before the interruption remain recorded, and employers do not need to send those returns again.

Employers who saw an error message during submission should check their filing history for a receipt number. If no receipt appears, they should reopen the saved return and submit it. The service logged 186 reports from employers, including businesses in Amberford and Kestrel Bay. Anyone still unable to file should contact the payroll support team and quote the message shown on screen.

title: Companies reminded to check records before September filing deadline
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service reminded companies with accounting years ending on 31 March 2026 that their corporate tax returns and balancing payments are due on 30 September. A return is still required where a company made a loss or has no further tax to pay.

As of 4 September, the service had received 8,420 of the 13,600 returns expected from this group. Companies can save an unfinished online return and come back to it. Saving a draft does not count as filing, and a payment receipt does not confirm that a return has been submitted.

Before submitting, companies should check the following details against their accounts. These checks address the errors most often reported by processing teams in Saltmarsh and Ostara.

The accounting period matches the period shown on the return.
Payments on account are entered against the correct company reference.
Claims for equipment allowances include the required supporting schedule.

title: Sales tax registration threshold rises to support smaller businesses
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service today published a sales tax rule raising the compulsory registration threshold from KRN 150,000 to KRN 180,000. The change takes effect on 1 October and applies to taxable sales measured over a rolling 12-month period. The sales tax rate remains 6 per cent.

Businesses already registered must continue collecting and reporting sales tax unless the service approves their removal from the register. A business with taxable sales below the new threshold may apply to leave, but should first check whether tax adjustments are required for stock or equipment it still holds.

An explanatory notice includes worked examples for shops, repair businesses and seasonal traders. Printed copies are available at revenue offices in Kestrel Bay, Ostara and Val-Brume. The service estimates that 2,300 registered businesses have annual taxable sales between the old and new thresholds. Eligibility depends on each business’s records, rather than its size or number of employees.

title: Revenue Service opens additional help desks for small employers
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service opened additional payroll tax help desks today in Saltmarsh and Amberford. The desks support employers completing their first return or correcting employee details. Each location has four advisers, with appointments available between 9 am and 4 pm.

Employers should bring their business registration number, payroll totals and records of tax already paid. Advisers can explain how to complete a return and check whether the required sections are filled in. They cannot prepare wage records on an employer’s behalf or accept payments in cash.

The service recorded 640 requests for first-return support during the first three weeks of August. Missing employee reference numbers were the most common problem. Employers outside the two cities can receive the same guidance by telephone, including assistance in French through the Val-Brume support team. There is no charge for either service.

title: Revenue Service reports progress on sales tax refunds
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service processed 92 per cent of complete sales tax refund claims within 15 working days during September. This compares with 86 per cent in August. September payments totalled KRN 18.4 million across 1,760 claims, including claims from manufacturers, wholesalers and building contractors.

The improvement followed the reassignment of six processing staff to the refund team in Ostara. Claims requiring further checks are excluded from the 15-day measure while the service waits for requested information. The published figures include both the number of claims awaiting checks and the reasons for those checks.

At the end of September, 214 claims were awaiting invoices, bank account confirmation or an explanation of unusually large purchases. Businesses can check progress through their tax account. Sending the same claim again can delay processing because staff must establish whether it is a duplicate. A business should instead reply to the information request using its existing claim reference.

title: Higher sales tax threshold now applies across Kestria
body:
The higher compulsory sales tax registration threshold of KRN 180,000 is now in force, the Kestria Revenue Service confirmed today. It took effect on 1 October, replacing the KRN 150,000 threshold. Businesses must measure their taxable sales over a rolling 12-month period when checking whether registration is required.

By the close of business on 2 October, the service had received 486 applications to leave the sales tax register. Of these, 312 had been approved and 174 remained under review. Each approved business received a notice stating the date from which it must stop charging sales tax.

The service reminded traders in Saltmarsh, Val-Brume and other communities that applying does not immediately end their obligations. Registered businesses must keep collecting tax and filing returns until their approved removal date. The sales tax rate remains 6 per cent. Customers can ask suppliers for a corrected invoice if tax has been charged after a supplier’s registration ended.

title: Employers receive clarification on payroll tax for travel payments
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service published a clarification today on payroll tax treatment of employee travel payments. It explains the existing distinction between reimbursing documented business travel and paying a fixed travel allowance. The clarification does not change the payroll tax rate or introduce a new charge.

A reimbursement matching a supported business travel expense can be excluded from taxable wages. A fixed allowance paid regardless of actual costs must be included. Ordinary travel between home and an employee’s usual workplace does not qualify as business travel under these rules.

For example, an Ostara repair firm may reimburse KRN 86 for an employee’s documented journey to a customer in Amberford without adding that reimbursement to taxable wages. A separate KRN 200 monthly travel allowance paid without expense records must be included. Employers should retain the journey’s purpose, date and supporting receipts. The guidance answers 143 travel-related enquiries received by the payroll support team during September.

title: Val-Brume revenue office introduces French payroll support appointments
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service introduced dedicated French-language payroll support appointments at its Val-Brume office today. The office now offers 24 appointments each week for employers who need help understanding returns, account balances or requests for information. Telephone support in French remains available.

The appointment service follows a local trial held during September, when advisers assisted 68 employers. Most enquiries concerned corrections to monthly wages and matching payments to the correct reporting period. Appointments last 30 minutes and can be booked by telephone or through a business tax account.

Employers should bring the relevant return, wage records and any letter they want to discuss. A representative attending for a business must have authority recorded on its tax account before staff can discuss private information. General guidance is available without access to an account. The service does not charge for appointments, and employers do not need to use a paid intermediary to book one.

title: September corporate tax filing figures show fewer late returns
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service received 12,716 corporate tax returns by the 30 September deadline from companies with accounting years ending on 31 March 2026. This represents 93.5 per cent of the 13,600 returns expected. The comparable filing rate for the previous year was 91.8 per cent.

The service has issued reminders to the 884 companies whose returns were outstanding at the deadline. Companies that have since filed can check their account for confirmation. A company that cannot pay its full balance should still submit its return and contact the service to discuss its position.

Support teams in Saltmarsh and Amberford are handling enquiries about outstanding filings. Companies contacting them should have the following information available so staff can identify the correct account and explain the next steps.

The company registration and tax reference numbers.
The accounting period covered by the missing return.
Any filing receipt or payment reference already received.

title: Revenue Service reports progress on sales tax refunds
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service processed 92 per cent of complete sales tax refund claims within 15 working days during September. This compares with 86 per cent in August. September payments totalled KRN 18.4 million across 1,760 claims, including claims from manufacturers, wholesalers and building contractors.

The improvement followed the reassignment of six processing staff to the refund team in Ostara. Claims requiring further checks are excluded from the 15-day measure while the service waits for requested information. The published figures include both the number of claims awaiting checks and the reasons for those checks.

At the end of September, 214 claims were awaiting invoices, bank account confirmation or an explanation of unusually large purchases. Businesses can check progress through their tax account. Sending the same claim again can delay processing because staff must establish whether it is a duplicate. A business should instead reply to the information request using its existing claim reference.

title: Higher sales tax threshold now applies across Kestria
body:
The higher compulsory sales tax registration threshold of KRN 180,000 is now in force, the Kestria Revenue Service confirmed today. It took effect on 1 October, replacing the KRN 150,000 threshold. Businesses must measure their taxable sales over a rolling 12-month period when checking whether registration is required.

By the close of business on 2 October, the service had received 486 applications to leave the sales tax register. Of these, 312 had been approved and 174 remained under review. Each approved business received a notice stating the date from which it must stop charging sales tax.

The service reminded traders in Saltmarsh, Val-Brume and other communities that applying does not immediately end their obligations. Registered businesses must keep collecting tax and filing returns until their approved removal date. The sales tax rate remains 6 per cent. Customers can ask suppliers for a corrected invoice if tax has been charged after a supplier’s registration ended.

title: New guidance explains October sales tax registration changes
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service has published further guidance on the sales tax registration threshold announced on 27 August. The compulsory threshold rises to KRN 180,000 on 1 October. The guidance answers questions received from 370 businesses through revenue offices and the telephone support service.

A business below the new threshold can remain registered voluntarily. If it chooses to apply for removal, it must continue charging sales tax until its approved removal date. Applications require current sales records, and approval is not automatic.

The guidance includes an example of a Kestrel Bay trader with rolling annual taxable sales of KRN 168,000. That trader may apply for removal under the new threshold, but must account for sales tax while still registered. Businesses preparing an application should have these records ready.

Monthly taxable sales for the latest 12 months.
Details of stock and equipment still held.
The requested removal date and business contact details.

title: Payroll corrections guide explains how to fix common errors
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service issued a payroll corrections guide today after reviewing 1,120 amended returns received in August. Almost half involved wages entered in the wrong reporting month. The guide explains how employers can correct a submitted return without creating a second charge for the same wages.

Employers should open the original return, select the correction option and enter the full replacement figures for the affected month. They should not enter only the difference between the old and correct amounts. Each accepted correction produces a new receipt linked to the original filing.

For example, an Amberford employer that reported taxable wages of KRN 42,000 instead of KRN 24,000 should replace the wages figure with KRN 24,000. Any resulting credit appears on the employer’s account after processing. The guide is available in English and French, with printed copies at the Val-Brume revenue office. Employers should keep records explaining why each correction was made.

title: Payroll filing service restored after morning access problems
body:
Access to the Kestria Revenue Service payroll filing service was restored at 11.40 am today following a technical fault. The interruption began at 8.15 am and affected employers trying to open or submit payroll tax returns. Corporate tax and sales tax filing remained available.

The fault interrupted the connection between the sign-in page and payroll records. Technical checks found no evidence that employer or employee information had been lost or disclosed. Returns submitted before the interruption remain recorded, and employers do not need to send those returns again.

Employers who saw an error message during submission should check their filing history for a receipt number. If no receipt appears, they should reopen the saved return and submit it. The service logged 186 reports from employers, including businesses in Amberford and Kestrel Bay. Anyone still unable to file should contact the payroll support team and quote the message shown on screen.

title: Revenue Service publishes results of employer account checks
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service has completed a review of 620 employer accounts selected because payroll returns and payments did not match. The review covered reporting periods from April to August 2026. Staff resolved 458 accounts without assessing additional tax, mainly by allocating payments to the correct month.

A further 112 employers corrected returns, producing KRN 740,000 in additional payroll tax due. Checks remain open on 50 accounts while staff examine wage records. The service said an account mismatch alone does not establish that an employer has underpaid tax.

Employers in Kestrel Bay and across Kestria can reduce avoidable enquiries by checking their account after each payment. Where a balance looks wrong, they should compare the return and bank record before contacting the service. Useful checks include the following.

Use the employer’s own tax reference when making a payment.
Check that the payment covers the intended reporting month.
Keep the filing receipt alongside the payment confirmation.

title: Employers receive clarification on payroll tax for travel payments
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service published a clarification today on payroll tax treatment of employee travel payments. It explains the existing distinction between reimbursing documented business travel and paying a fixed travel allowance. The clarification does not change the payroll tax rate or introduce a new charge.

A reimbursement matching a supported business travel expense can be excluded from taxable wages. A fixed allowance paid regardless of actual costs must be included. Ordinary travel between home and an employee’s usual workplace does not qualify as business travel under these rules.

For example, an Ostara repair firm may reimburse KRN 86 for an employee’s documented journey to a customer in Amberford without adding that reimbursement to taxable wages. A separate KRN 200 monthly travel allowance paid without expense records must be included. Employers should retain the journey’s purpose, date and supporting receipts. The guidance answers 143 travel-related enquiries received by the payroll support team during September.

title: Val-Brume revenue office introduces French payroll support appointments
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service introduced dedicated French-language payroll support appointments at its Val-Brume office today. The office now offers 24 appointments each week for employers who need help understanding returns, account balances or requests for information. Telephone support in French remains available.

The appointment service follows a local trial held during September, when advisers assisted 68 employers. Most enquiries concerned corrections to monthly wages and matching payments to the correct reporting period. Appointments last 30 minutes and can be booked by telephone or through a business tax account.

Employers should bring the relevant return, wage records and any letter they want to discuss. A representative attending for a business must have authority recorded on its tax account before staff can discuss private information. General guidance is available without access to an account. The service does not charge for appointments, and employers do not need to use a paid intermediary to book one.

title: September corporate tax filing figures show fewer late returns
body:
The Kestria Revenue Service received 12,716 corporate tax returns by the 30 September deadline from companies with accounting years ending on 31 March 2026. This represents 93.5 per cent of the 13,600 returns expected. The comparable filing rate for the previous year was 91.8 per cent.

The service has issued reminders to the 884 companies whose returns were outstanding at the deadline. Companies that have since filed can check their account for confirmation. A company that cannot pay its full balance should still submit its return and contact the service to discuss its position.

Support teams in Saltmarsh and Amberford are handling enquiries about outstanding filings. Companies contacting them should have the following information available so staff can identify the correct account and explain the next steps.

The company registration and tax reference numbers.
The accounting period covered by the missing return.
Any filing receipt or payment reference already received.

title: Corrected Amberford Heatworks report satisfies Commission disclosure direction
author: Selin Arvane
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission has completed its review of the corrected half-year report published by Amberford Heatworks on 8 September. The revised report satisfies the disclosure direction announced on 25 August concerning a loan condition linked to the company's minimum cash reserves.

The corrected report explains the KRN 6 million cash threshold, how the lender measures compliance and when repayment could be demanded. It also sets out the company's cash position at 30 June and the steps management would consider if reserves approached the threshold. The company published the required separate notice explaining the corrections.

The Commission is closing its review of compliance with this direction. This does not amount to an assessment of the company's financial strength or a recommendation to buy its bonds. The case underlines the need to explain borrowing conditions alongside headline debt figures. Issuers should check that investors can understand both when obligations fall due and what could cause payment dates to change.

title: Commission reminds issuers of approaching annual reporting consultation deadline
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission is reminding interested parties that its consultation on clearer annual reporting closes on 29 September. The consultation, opened on 18 August, covers explanations of funding risks, major customer losses and changes to accounting estimates in listed company reports.

The Commission has received 26 submissions so far, including responses from individual investors and smaller listed companies. Several respondents have asked how much detail would be expected when a company depends on one large customer. The consultation paper includes questions on this issue, and further views are welcome.

Respondents may answer any of the questions and do not need to comment on the whole paper. Submissions can be made in English or French. Anyone requesting confidential treatment should identify the relevant passages and explain why confidentiality is needed. The Commission will consider the evidence before deciding its next steps. Existing reporting requirements continue to apply while the proposals are under review.

title: Kestrel Bay broker fined for trading ahead of client orders
author: Dorian Pellac
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission has imposed a KRN 780,000 penalty on Kestrel Bay broker Velmora Securities for using confidential client order information when trading for its own account. The firm admitted the breaches and agreed to appoint an independent reviewer of its trading controls.

Between February and May, a trading desk bought shares before executing 23 large client purchase orders. It then sold those shares after the client purchases had pushed prices higher. The conduct generated KRN 164,000 in profits. The firm must return that amount to affected clients in addition to paying the penalty.

The investigation found that staff could view pending client orders while placing trades for the firm's account, without effective checks. Velmora Securities has restricted that access. Its independent reviewer must assess the changes and report to the Commission within 90 days. The firm must also provide clients with a written explanation of how individual repayment amounts were calculated.

title: Commission publishes findings from review of market announcement timing
author: Selin Arvane
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission has completed a review of how quickly listed companies publish information that could affect their securities prices. Staff examined 63 announcements issued between January and June, including notices about cancelled contracts, financing agreements and significant changes to expected earnings.

In 11 cases, companies could not provide a clear record of when senior staff first received the information. Five companies relied on a single person to approve announcements, with no cover during absences. The Commission has written to those companies requesting improvements to their procedures.

The findings do not establish that all 11 companies disclosed information late. However, incomplete records make it harder to demonstrate compliance. Companies should record key decisions, identify an alternative approver and keep disclosure arrangements under review. A briefing note published today includes practical examples. The Commission will assess the responses before deciding whether any individual case requires further investigation.

title: Amberford bond issuer ordered to correct missing debt disclosures
author: Dorian Pellac
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission has directed Amberford Heatworks to correct its latest half-year report after the bond issuer omitted information about a loan condition. The condition allows a lender to demand repayment if the company's cash reserves fall below KRN 6 million.

The company reported cash reserves of KRN 7.4 million at 30 June but did not explain the condition or the consequences of breaching it. The Commission considers this information necessary for investors assessing the company's ability to meet payments on its KRN 42 million bond issue.

Amberford Heatworks must publish a corrected report by 8 September and explain the changes in a separate market notice. The direction does not require early repayment of the bonds. No financial penalty has been imposed. The Commission will review the corrected report and consider whether further action is needed. Bond issuers remain responsible for explaining significant borrowing conditions in plain language.

title: Commission opens consultation on clearer reporting by listed companies
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission today opened a consultation on proposed changes to annual reporting rules for listed companies. The proposals would require clearer explanations of cash shortages, major customer losses and changes to accounting estimates. Responses must reach the Commission by 29 September 2026.

A review of 48 annual reports found that 17 companies used broad statements that gave investors little information about their main risks. Nine reports described available funding without explaining when loans fell due. The proposed rules would require companies to connect these figures with their plans for meeting payments.

The consultation also asks whether smaller issuers should receive additional guidance and a longer preparation period. Investors, companies, auditors and other interested parties may submit written comments. The consultation paper is available in English and French. The Commission has not decided whether to adopt the proposals and will publish a summary of responses.

title: Ostara workshop will explain bond disclosure duties to smaller issuers
author: Lucien Marcelet
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission will hold a free workshop in Ostara on 22 October for smaller companies that issue bonds to the public. The session will explain continuing disclosure duties, including how to report borrowing conditions, missed payments and material changes in available funding.

There are 60 places available, with registration closing on 19 October unless the session fills earlier. Finance staff, company secretaries and directors may attend. Commission staff will use fictional examples involving a KRN 15 million bond issue and a loan approaching its repayment date. Attendance does not satisfy any formal reporting requirement.

Participants may submit general questions when registering. Staff cannot give advance approval to company announcements or discuss confidential supervisory cases at the workshop. Written materials will be available in English and French, and a French-language online session will be arranged separately. The Commission will publish the presentation materials so that issuers unable to attend can use the same guidance.

title: Annual reporting consultation closes with forty three written submissions
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission received 43 written submissions to its consultation on clearer annual reporting, which closed on 29 September. Non-confidential responses are now available in the consultation register. Staff are reviewing the evidence, and no decision has been made on changes to the rules.

The submissions came from 16 listed companies, 12 individual investors, seven audit practices and eight other respondents. Common topics included the cost of preparing additional explanations, the treatment of commercially sensitive customer information and the time smaller companies would need to update reporting procedures.

Several investors requested clearer links between borrowing figures and repayment dates. Some companies favoured practical guidance alongside any new requirements. The Commission will assess these views together rather than treating the number of responses supporting a proposal as a vote. A response paper will explain the conclusions and any proposed implementation arrangements. Companies should continue to prepare reports under the existing rules.

title: Commission seeks court order over suspected false revenue statements
author: Dorian Pellac
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission has applied to the securities court in Saltmarsh for an order requiring Ordelune Storage to preserve accounting records and related correspondence. The application forms part of an investigation into suspected false revenue statements in the listed company's latest annual report.

The Commission is examining whether KRN 18.6 million recorded as storage service revenue was supported by completed work. Its application concerns records held by the company and two former executives. The Commission has asked for an expedited hearing because some relevant electronic records are subject to routine deletion.

The allegations have not been determined by the court. The application does not seek a finding of liability or a financial penalty at this stage. Ordelune Storage and the former executives will have an opportunity to respond. The Commission will publish a further update when the court decides the application. Investors should consult the company's market announcements for its statements on the matter.

title: Court orders preservation of records in Ordelune Storage investigation
author: Dorian Pellac
body:
The securities court in Saltmarsh today ordered Ordelune Storage and two former executives to preserve records relevant to the Kestria Securities Commission's investigation into suspected false revenue statements. The order follows the Commission's application announced on 13 October and takes effect immediately.

The order covers accounting entries, customer contracts, invoices and related correspondence concerning KRN 18.6 million in reported storage service revenue. Those subject to it must suspend routine deletion of relevant electronic material and retain paper records. They must provide written confirmation of the preservation steps taken within seven days.

The court has not decided whether the revenue statements were false or whether any person breached securities law. The Commission's investigation continues, and the company and former executives retain the right to respond to any allegations. Preserving the records will allow the evidence to be examined. The Commission will announce any further public proceedings when they are filed.

title: Val-Brume review finds gaps in French bond disclosure documents
author: Lucien Marcelet
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission has asked six bond issuers to correct French disclosure documents following a review in Val-Brume. Staff examined 28 documents made available to investors in the French-speaking region and compared key payment terms with the corresponding English versions.

Four documents omitted wording about an issuer's right to repay bonds early. Two others gave an incorrect deadline for bondholders to submit payment instructions. The affected issues have a combined face value of KRN 96 million. The review did not identify any payment already missed because of these errors.

The six issuers must publish corrected documents and notify affected holders by 30 October. The Commission has also requested evidence of checks by staff with suitable language and financial knowledge. Issuers remain responsible for the accuracy of documents prepared by outside translators. Investors who believe a discrepancy has affected a payment should contact the issuer and may also report the matter to the Commission.

Ordelune Storage and the former executives will have an opportunity to respond. The Commission will publish a further update when the court decides the application. Investors should consult the company's market announcements for its statements on the matter.

title: Ostara workshop will explain bond disclosure duties to smaller issuers
author: Lucien Marcelet
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission will hold a free workshop in Ostara on 22 October for smaller companies that issue bonds to the public. The session will explain continuing disclosure duties, including how to report borrowing conditions, missed payments and material changes in available funding.

There are 60 places available, with registration closing on 19 October unless the session fills earlier. Finance staff, company secretaries and directors may attend. Commission staff will use fictional examples involving a KRN 15 million bond issue and a loan approaching its repayment date. Attendance does not satisfy any formal reporting requirement.

Participants may submit general questions when registering. Staff cannot give advance approval to company announcements or discuss confidential supervisory cases at the workshop. Written materials will be available in English and French, and a French-language online session will be arranged separately. The Commission will publish the presentation materials so that issuers unable to attend can use the same guidance.

title: Corrected Amberford Heatworks report satisfies Commission disclosure direction
author: Selin Arvane
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission has completed its review of the corrected half-year report published by Amberford Heatworks on 8 September. The revised report satisfies the disclosure direction announced on 25 August concerning a loan condition linked to the company's minimum cash reserves.

The corrected report explains the KRN 6 million cash threshold, how the lender measures compliance and when repayment could be demanded. It also sets out the company's cash position at 30 June and the steps management would consider if reserves approached the threshold. The company published the required separate notice explaining the corrections.

The Commission is closing its review of compliance with this direction. This does not amount to an assessment of the company's financial strength or a recommendation to buy its bonds. The case underlines the need to explain borrowing conditions alongside headline debt figures. Issuers should check that investors can understand both when obligations fall due and what could cause payment dates to change.

title: Commission reminds issuers of approaching annual reporting consultation deadline
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission is reminding interested parties that its consultation on clearer annual reporting closes on 29 September. The consultation, opened on 18 August, covers explanations of funding risks, major customer losses and changes to accounting estimates in listed company reports.

The Commission has received 26 submissions so far, including responses from individual investors and smaller listed companies. Several respondents have asked how much detail would be expected when a company depends on one large customer. The consultation paper includes questions on this issue, and further views are welcome.

Respondents may answer any of the questions and do not need to comment on the whole paper. Submissions can be made in English or French. Anyone requesting confidential treatment should identify the relevant passages and explain why confidentiality is needed. The Commission will consider the evidence before deciding its next steps. Existing reporting requirements continue to apply while the proposals are under review.

title: Kestrel Bay broker fined for trading ahead of client orders
author: Dorian Pellac
body:
The Kestria Securities Commission has imposed a KRN 780,000 penalty on Kestrel Bay broker Velmora Securities for using confidential client order information when trading for its own account. The firm admitted the breaches and agreed to appoint an independent reviewer of its trading controls.

Between February and May, a trading desk bought shares before executing 23 large client purchase orders. It then sold those shares after the client purchases had pushed prices higher. The conduct generated KRN 164,000 in profits. The firm must return that amount to affected clients in addition to paying the penalty.

The investigation found that staff could view pending client orders while placing trades for the firm's account, without effective checks. Velmora Securities has restricted that access. Its independent reviewer must assess the changes and report to the Commission within 90 days. The firm must also provide clients with a written explanation of how individual repayment amounts were calculated.

title: Council approves revenue amendments following public September meeting
author: Tomas Elwick
body:
The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria approved amendments to Kestrian Accounting Standard 8, Revenue from Customer Contracts, at its public meeting on 16 September. All seven members present voted in favour, subject to final drafting checks.

Clearer treatment of contract changes

The amendments clarify when a change to agreed goods and prices forms a separate contract. They also explain when a company must update revenue already recognised. The Council considered 27 consultation responses and retained the proposed accounting approach.

Additional examples for staged deliveries
Clearer allocation of revised prices
Transition relief for completed contracts

Publication is planned for 6 October. The approved effective date is annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with early application permitted once the amendments are issued. The published text will set out the transition method and required disclosures. Companies should continue using the current published standard until the amendments are available.

title: Supplier finance consultation enters its final response period
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria is reminding companies and users of accounts that comments on its supplier finance proposals close on 30 September. As at 18 September, the Council had received 16 written responses.

Evidence still sought

Early responses identify practical questions about obtaining information from finance providers. The Council is seeking further evidence on the time and cost involved, particularly where a company uses several providers or has arrangements covering suppliers in different parts of Kestria.

Availability of opening balance information
Time needed to change reporting systems
Usefulness of payment date ranges
Costs of gathering comparative figures

title: Council corrects illustrative lease example without changing requirements
author: Luc Morevaux
body:
The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has corrected a numerical error in the illustrative examples accompanying Kestrian Accounting Standard 11, Leases. The correction affects Example 6 in the supporting booklet published in June 2026.

Corrected payment total

The example describes equipment leased by a fictional workshop in Amberford. Four annual payments of KRN 24,000 were correctly shown in the payment schedule, but the accompanying sentence gave their total as KRN 94,000. That sentence now states KRN 96,000.

Payment schedule remains unchanged
Discounted calculations remain unchanged
Explanatory sentence has been corrected

The revised booklet is labelled September 2026 and includes a correction note beside the example. This is an editorial correction to supporting material, so it has no effective date or transition provisions. Companies do not need to change their accounting policies because of it. Printed copies distributed at Council workshops will include the corrected page.

title: September meeting papers cover revenue and reporting priorities
author: Tomas Elwick
body:
The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published papers for its public meeting in Saltmarsh on 16 September. The meeting will consider proposed clarifications to Kestrian Accounting Standard 8, Revenue from Customer Contracts, and priorities for the next reporting cycle.

Items for discussion

Staff have analysed 27 responses to the revenue consultation, which closed on 31 July. Respondents generally supported clearer treatment of contract changes, although several requested more detail on allocating revised prices to goods already delivered.

Revenue consultation findings
Examples involving revised contract prices
Research on smaller company disclosures
Progress against the annual work plan

The papers recommend amendments for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, but no decision has been made. Public observers may reserve one of 30 seats by 14 September. A written decision summary will be published after the meeting, including any changes to the staff recommendations.

title: Autumn workshop programme opens for company accounts teams
author: Celia Brackenwell
body:
The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has opened registration for four autumn workshops on applying existing accounting requirements. Each session will offer 45 places, with attendance free of charge.

Practical sessions across Kestria

The programme covers Saltmarsh on 10 September, Kestrel Bay on 17 September, Ostara on 24 September and Val-Brume on 1 October. The Val-Brume session will be delivered in French, with the same worked examples and supporting material as the other sessions.

Recognising revenue from staged deliveries
Estimating provisions for repairs
Presenting material accounting policies
Recording questions for Council staff

Participants may submit questions when registering. Staff will use those questions to select examples, including transactions valued between KRN 20,000 and KRN 500,000. The workshops explain current standards and do not create additional requirements. Places will be allocated in order of registration, initially limited to two people from each company or practice.

title: Council seeks views on clearer supplier finance disclosures
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published proposed amendments to Kestrian Accounting Standard 14, Cash Flows and Financing. The proposals would require companies to explain arrangements under which a finance provider pays suppliers and the company later pays that provider.

Information proposed

The draft would introduce a single note showing the size and main terms of these arrangements. Companies would retain responsibility for deciding how the related liabilities and cash flows are classified under existing requirements.

Opening and closing liability balances
Amounts already paid to suppliers
Ranges of payment due dates
Significant changes without cash movements

Comments are invited by 30 September 2026. The Council particularly welcomes examples from manufacturers and wholesalers in Amberford and Ostara. Its initial proposal is for annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2028, with early application permitted. The final requirements and transition arrangements will depend on the evidence received.

title: Workshop report identifies recurring questions from accounts preparers
author: Celia Brackenwell
body:
The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published a report on its four autumn workshops. A total of 163 people attended sessions in Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara and Val-Brume between 10 September and 1 October.

Questions informing future support

Participants submitted 58 questions before the sessions and raised further examples during discussion. Staff grouped the questions by topic, with revenue recognition and repair provisions accounting for just over half of the advance submissions.

Evidence supporting repair estimates
Revenue from partly completed deliveries
Choosing useful accounting policy information
Explaining changes in estimates

The report summarises recurring difficulties and includes six examples drawn from the sessions, with company details replaced by invented facts. It explains the standards in force during the workshops. The revenue amendments issued on 6 October are available separately. Staff will use the findings when proposing next year's educational programme; the report itself introduces no accounting requirements.

title: Revenue amendments issued with relief for completed contracts
author: Tomas Elwick
body:

No restatement of comparative figures

title: New supplier finance disclosures include first year transition relief
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has issued amendments to Kestrian Accounting Standard 14, Cash Flows and Financing, following approval at its meeting on 14 October. The amendments require a note explaining supplier finance arrangements and their effect on company liabilities.

Requirements from 2028

The amendments apply to annual periods beginning on or after 1 January 2028, with early application permitted and disclosed. The note must describe key terms, opening and closing liabilities, amounts already paid to suppliers, payment date ranges and significant changes without cash movements.

Comparatives waived in the first year
Opening balances waived in the first year
Closing balances required from initial application
Existing classification requirements retained

The Council added transition relief after considering 34 consultation responses. For a calendar-year company first applying the amendments in 2028, the initial note will therefore include its closing position at 31 December 2028 without corresponding 2027 figures. The publication includes a scope example involving an Amberford wholesaler.

title: Council publishes supplier finance feedback ahead of decision
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published a summary of responses to its proposed supplier finance disclosures. The consultation closed on 30 September with 34 responses from companies, lenders, accounts users and accounting practices.

Support and implementation concerns

Twenty-six respondents supported a single note bringing together information about these arrangements. Several companies said that opening balances and comparative figures would be costly to obtain for the first year, especially where finance providers hold part of the information.

Broad support for closing balances
Requests for clearer scope wording
Concerns about comparative information
Support for a 2028 effective date

The Council will consider the proposals at its public meeting in Saltmarsh on 14 October. Staff recommend retaining the proposed annual effective date and adding first-year relief for opening balances and comparatives. These are recommendations only. The Council has not yet approved final amendments, and companies should continue applying the existing standard.

author: Tomas Elwick
body:
The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria has published its operating update for the nine months ended 30 September 2026. Expenditure totalled KRN 3.42 million against a phased budget of KRN 3.60 million.

Resources and delivery

The KRN 180,000 difference mainly reflects vacant research posts and lower venue costs. Technical staffing stood at 18 filled posts out of 20 at the period end. The update also records progress on consultations, educational material and public access to Council meetings.

Revenue amendments issued in October
Supplier finance amendments issued in October
Smaller company research recruitment opened
Intangible assets research timetable revised

The Council now expects to publish its preliminary intangible assets research paper in February 2027, two months later than previously planned. Staff time has been reassigned to complete the current amendments and support their introduction. The timetable change does not alter any accounting requirement or effective date. The full-year operating budget remains KRN 4.80 million.

title: Research invitation focuses on smaller company reporting costs
author: Celia Brackenwell
body:
The Accounting Standards Council of Kestria is inviting smaller companies to join a research study on the cost of preparing annual accounts. The study will inform its work plan and does not propose changes to any standard.

Thirty companies sought

Staff aim to recruit 30 companies with annual revenue between KRN 2 million and KRN 40 million. The sample will cover manufacturing, retail and services, with participants sought in Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara, Amberford and Val-Brume.

Hours spent gathering supporting records
Costs of external accounting advice
Disclosures requiring substantial judgement
Information used by lenders and owners

Expressions of interest close on 13 November 2026. Selected participants will be asked to complete one questionnaire and attend a 60-minute interview in English or French. Findings will be published in grouped form, without naming participating companies. The Council will assess the evidence before deciding whether any reporting topic needs further research or public consultation.
