title: Oakhill Opens Recruitment for New Kestrel Bay Bakery
author: Rowan Pellwick
body:
Oakhill Bakeries Group has opened recruitment for 46 permanent roles at its new Kestrel Bay bakery. Vacancies cover production, engineering, hygiene, warehousing and supervision. Construction is complete, and equipment testing is under way. The site is not yet producing goods for sale.

The bakery has a designed capacity of 20 tonnes a day and contains separate areas for bread rolls and morning goods. Oakhill has invested KRN 13.6 million in the building and equipment. Applications are open to experienced bakery workers and candidates seeking their first manufacturing role.

Production roles start at KRN 17.40 an hour, with additional payments for night work. Each vacancy states its shift pattern and guaranteed hours. Staff affected by the Ostara closure proposal can request a confidential discussion about these roles without giving up their right to take part in the consultation.

title: Oakhill Introduces Clearer Delivery Charges for Small Shops
author: Lucien Bréval
body:
Oakhill Bakeries Group has introduced a single delivery charge for small shop orders across its existing delivery network in Kestria. Orders below KRN 240 now carry a KRN 12 charge. Orders at or above that value receive delivery without a separate fee.

The change replaces six local charging arrangements that had developed as delivery routes expanded. Product prices are unchanged. Customers received individual notices and examples showing how the revised charge applies to their usual orders, including mixed orders of bread, rolls and sweet bakery products.

The same threshold applies in Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara, Amberford and Val-Brume. Customers can combine products on one order to reach it. Commercial manager Nerys Fennholt said the simpler arrangement makes invoices easier to check and helps shopkeepers compare the cost of placing several small orders with one larger delivery.

title: Oakhill Holds Standard Loaf Price During Seasonal Range Launch
author: Lucien Bréval
body:
Oakhill Bakeries Group has launched three seasonal products while retaining the wholesale price of its standard 800g white loaf at KRN 4.23. The new range consists of a spiced apple bun, a pear-filled pastry and a round oat loaf, available to order from today.

Wholesale prices are KRN 8.40 for six apple buns, KRN 10.20 for six pear pastries and KRN 5.60 for one 600g oat loaf. Product sheets include ingredients, allergens and storage guidance. French language versions are available for customers in Val-Brume and the surrounding region.

Amberford produces the oat loaf, Saltmarsh makes the pear pastry and Kestrel Bay supplies the apple bun. The range uses existing equipment and is included in current production schedules. Commercial manager Nerys Fennholt said the launch gives shops more choice alongside everyday bread, with no additional change to the core wholesale price list.

title: Kestrel Bay Adds Second Shift as Bakery Orders Grow
author: Rowan Pellwick
body:
Oakhill Bakeries Group has introduced a second production shift at Kestrel Bay, taking average daily output from six to 12 tonnes. The bakery now supplies 91 shops and catering customers. Its designed daily capacity remains 20 tonnes, leaving room within the existing equipment.

Ten additional permanent employees have joined the site, bringing its workforce to 56. The new starters cover production, packing and hygiene roles. All have completed their initial safety and food hygiene training, with supervised equipment training continuing as part of their normal paid shifts.

The extra shift supports transferred Ostara orders and new business around Kestrel Bay. Bakery manager Dorian Kelwick said the team has added volume gradually while checking product consistency and delivery accuracy. The site recorded 98.7 per cent of order lines supplied in full during its first complete week of commercial production.

title: Oakhill Reports Lower Bread Waste Across Its Operating Bakeries
author: Mara Denholt
body:
Oakhill Bakeries Group reduced bread production waste to 2.8 per cent of baked weight in September, down from 3.6 per cent in June. The comparison covers Amberford, Saltmarsh and Ostara, which operated during both months. It excludes the new Kestrel Bay bakery.

The measure includes misshapen loaves, products damaged during packing and bread rejected during quality checks. It does not include unsold goods returned by shops, which Oakhill records separately. Production waste across the three sites fell from 54 tonnes in June to 43 tonnes in September.

Teams adjusted dough portion settings, improved checks at shift changes and replaced worn guides on two packing lines. Operations director Brenna Halewick said these small changes reduced avoidable losses without relaxing product standards. Site teams review the figures weekly, using weighing records and production totals to identify where further checks are needed.

title: Val-Brume Customers Receive Updated French Language Product Information
author: Lucien Bréval
body:
Oakhill Bakeries Group has issued updated French language product sheets for customers in Val-Brume and the surrounding French-speaking region. The sheets cover 34 products and bring ingredients, allergens, pack sizes and storage instructions into one consistent format for shop staff and catering teams.

The update follows customer feedback that older documents used different layouts and made pack sizes difficult to find. Each sheet now includes a product code, revision date and a clear statement of the number of items in a case. Recipes and wholesale prices are unchanged.

Printed copies are available through delivery drivers, alongside electronic versions from the customer service team. French-speaking staff checked the wording against current production specifications. Commercial manager Nerys Fennholt said the clearer information helps customers answer routine questions at the counter and identify the correct product when placing or checking an order.

title: Ostara Bakery Ends Production as Staff Transfers Take Effect
author: Elin Veymar
body:
Production has ended at Oakhill Bakeries Group's Ostara bakery. The final shift completed its orders yesterday, and the site is closed for baking from today. Customer orders have been transferred to Amberford and Kestrel Bay, with no changes to agreed delivery days.

Of the 31 employees affected, 19 have transferred within the group and 12 have left through redundancy. Transferring staff include 11 colleagues joining Amberford and eight already working at Kestrel Bay. All departing employees have received written confirmation of their final pay and redundancy arrangements.

A small facilities team is securing the building and recording equipment for removal or reuse. No decision has been made about the property's longer-term use. Managing director Tessa Oakhill thanked the Ostara team for completing the final orders carefully and supporting colleagues during the transfer of products and production records.

title: Kestrel Bay Bakery Starts Production With Local Delivery Orders
author: Mara Denholt
body:
Oakhill Bakeries Group's new Kestrel Bay bakery began commercial production today, supplying plain rolls and breakfast buns to 38 local shops. Opening output is six tonnes a day against a designed daily capacity of 20 tonnes. Orders are being added in stages as production settles.

The site employs 46 people, including eight colleagues transferring from Ostara. The team completed training, trial batches and cleaning checks before today's opening. Each production run is checked for weight, appearance and packing quality before goods are released for delivery to customers.

The KRN 13.6 million bakery has loading bays that keep incoming ingredients separate from finished goods. Bakery manager Dorian Kelwick said starting with a limited range gives staff time to establish consistent routines. Customers receiving their first deliveries have a dedicated contact for reporting shortages, damaged packs or concerns about product quality.

title: Gas network ruling disallows unsupported maintenance costs
body:
The Kestria Energy Board has disallowed KRN 1.8 million of maintenance costs claimed by the Saltmarsh gas network operator. The ruling follows a review of expenditure for the year ended 30 June. The operator did not provide sufficient work records to support costs assigned to 23 maintenance jobs.

The disputed amount forms part of a KRN 41.6 million maintenance claim. The Board accepted KRN 39.8 million after checking invoices, inspection records and staff time entries. The disallowed costs cannot be recovered through regulated network charges. This decision does not alter the tariff currently shown on customer bills.

The ruling concerns evidence supporting expenditure. It makes no finding that the maintenance itself was unnecessary or that the network is unsafe. The operator must keep clearer records linking each charge to completed work. A summary of the assessment explains the evidence requirements and lists the categories of costs that were excluded.

title: Ostara industrial gas restrictions lifted after equipment repairs
body:
Supply restrictions on the East Ostara industrial gas branch have been lifted following repairs to a pressure regulator. The Kestria Energy Board confirmed the change after reviewing test records supplied by the network operator. The branch has returned to its normal available capacity of 92 megawatt hours per hour.

The restrictions affected 14 sites with interruptible supply agreements from 22 September. The operator recorded a total requested reduction of 16 megawatt hours per hour during the restriction period. It has reported no interruption to household supplies and no loss of gas containment associated with the equipment fault.

Affected businesses have received individual notices cancelling their temporary limits. The Board has requested maintenance records and an explanation of how the fault developed. This review is separate from the decision to restore capacity. Businesses disputing a charge connected with the restriction should first use their supplier's complaints process and retain their meter records.

title: Industrial gas users in Ostara receive pressure advisory
body:
The Kestria Energy Board has issued a supply advisory for large gas users connected to the East Ostara industrial branch. A pressure regulator fault identified this morning has reduced the branch's available capacity from 92 to 76 megawatt hours per hour. Household gas connections are unaffected.

The network operator has contacted the 14 sites holding interruptible supply agreements on the branch. Under those agreements, affected sites must keep within the individual limits stated in their notices. The Board has confirmed that the combined reduction requested from these sites is 16 megawatt hours per hour.

Engineering staff are assessing the faulty equipment. No loss of gas containment has been reported. Other industrial customers should continue to follow their existing supply terms and should not change equipment settings on the basis of this advisory alone. The Board's industrial supply desk is recording operational difficulties reported by affected sites.

title: Board clarifies billing rules following household tariff reduction
body:
The Kestria Energy Board has issued billing guidance following the household electricity standing charge reduction on 15 September. The guidance addresses questions received from customers and suppliers about bills covering days on both sides of the change. It does not introduce another tariff change.

For a bill covering 1 to 30 September, suppliers must charge 14 days at KRN 0.84 and 16 days at KRN 0.79. The standing charge for that period is therefore KRN 24.40. Electricity used during the period remains subject to the unchanged unit rate of KRN 0.246 per kilowatt hour.

Customers using advance credit meters are also entitled to the lower standing charge from 15 September. Where a meter update has taken longer, suppliers must credit the difference. The Board has asked suppliers to keep records of these adjustments so its billing team can check that customers receive the full reduction.

title: Electricity tariff decision reduces standard household standing charge
body:
The Kestria Energy Board has approved a reduction in the standard household electricity standing charge from KRN 0.84 to KRN 0.79 a day. The decision applies from today to customers on the regulated standard tariff. The electricity unit rate remains KRN 0.246 per kilowatt hour.

The reduction reflects lower verified costs for billing and customer account administration. For a household remaining on the tariff for a full 365 days, the standing charge difference is KRN 18.25. Actual bills still depend on consumption, meter readings and any separate credits or charges shown on the account.

Suppliers must show the revised standing charge clearly and divide billing periods where they cross the change date. Customers do not need to apply for the reduction. The Board examined cost returns from all six licensed household suppliers before reaching its decision. Network charges are unchanged by this ruling.

title: Board publishes annual review of electricity network charges
body:
The Kestria Energy Board has published its annual review of electricity network charges. The review covers the cost of carrying power to homes and businesses across Kestria. It records KRN 184 million in allowed network revenue for the year ended 30 June, against actual spending of KRN 179 million.

Most of the difference came from delayed cable replacement in Amberford and lower maintenance costs around Saltmarsh. The Board has required network operators to explain how the unspent allowance is recorded in their accounts. Operators cannot treat money allowed for unfinished work as an unrestricted surplus.

The review does not change customer tariffs. It also reports that average electricity interruptions fell from 74 minutes to 68 minutes per customer over the year. Rural districts west of Ostara remained above that average, at 112 minutes. The full review includes separate spending and service tables for each network area.

title: Amberford electricity connection delays prompt formal improvement notice
body:
The Kestria Energy Board has issued a formal improvement notice to the Amberford electricity network operator after an audit found repeated delays in providing connection quotations. Of 160 complete applications examined, 47 had not received a quotation within the required 15 working days.

The applications covered small shops, workshops and housing developments. The longest recorded wait was 38 working days. The operator attributed the backlog to vacancies and incomplete internal handovers. The Board found that these problems did not remove its obligation to meet the published service standard.

The notice requires weekly reporting of outstanding quotations and a named contact for every affected applicant. It also requires the operator to separate applications awaiting customer information from those delayed within its own teams. The notice imposes no financial penalty. Applicants can ask the operator for a written explanation of their case and use the Board's complaints route if it remains unresolved.

body:

title: Val-Brume office expands access to energy billing advice
body:
The Kestria Energy Board's Val-Brume office has introduced an additional weekly session for customers seeking help with electricity and gas bills. The service provides advice in French and English. It covers tariff explanations, estimated readings, disputed charges and the steps involved in making a formal complaint.

The additional session follows a rise in local enquiries from 86 in July to 129 in September. Most concerned estimated bills and difficulties obtaining account corrections. Customers can bring a recent bill, relevant meter readings and copies of messages already exchanged with their supplier. There is no charge for the service.

Staff can explain the rules and help customers identify the information needed to pursue a case. They cannot change a meter reading or promise a particular complaint outcome during an advice session. The office's published service information includes accessible appointment options and arrangements for customers who need someone to speak on their behalf.

title: Meter checks find errors in industrial electricity bills
body:
A Kestria Energy Board audit has identified incorrect meter multipliers on nine industrial electricity accounts in Kestrel Bay. A multiplier converts the meter's recorded reading into the amount of electricity supplied. Using the wrong value can produce an incorrect bill even when the meter itself works properly.

Seven accounts were overcharged by a combined KRN 286,400 over periods ranging from four to eleven months. Two accounts were undercharged by a combined KRN 31,700. The supplier has accepted the findings and issued corrected account statements. All nine affected businesses have been contacted individually.

The Board has required repayment of the overcharges and a check of the supplier's remaining industrial meter settings. Any recovery of undercharges remains subject to the applicable billing rules and complaint rights. The audit found an account configuration problem, with no evidence of a fault in the physical meters or an interruption to electricity supply.

title: Quarterly report records fewer unresolved energy billing complaints
body:

Billing accounted for 61 per cent of new complaints. The most common issues were estimated consumption, delayed corrections and unclear account balances. Connection delays accounted for a further 17 per cent. The figures cover cases brought to the Board after customers had first raised the matter with their supplier or network operator.

The median time taken to close a case was 19 working days, compared with 23 in the preceding quarter. The Board cautions that a closed case does not always mean a complaint was upheld. Its tables distinguish corrections, explanations, withdrawn cases and formal findings so readers can see how complaints were resolved.

The restrictions affected 14 sites with interruptible supply agreements from 22 September. The operator recorded a total requested reduction of 16 megawatt hours per hour during the restriction period. It has reported no interruption to household supplies and no loss of gas containment associated with the equipment fault.

Affected businesses have received individual notices cancelling their temporary limits. The Board has requested maintenance records and an explanation of how the fault developed. This review is separate from the decision to restore capacity. Businesses disputing a charge connected with the restriction should first use their supplier's complaints process and retain their meter records.

title: Industrial gas users in Ostara receive pressure advisory
body:

The network operator has contacted the 14 sites holding interruptible supply agreements on the branch. Under those agreements, affected sites must keep within the individual limits stated in their notices. The Board has confirmed that the combined reduction requested from these sites is 16 megawatt hours per hour.

Engineering staff are assessing the faulty equipment. No loss of gas containment has been reported. Other industrial customers should continue to follow their existing supply terms and should not change equipment settings on the basis of this advisory alone. The Board's industrial supply desk is recording operational difficulties reported by affected sites.

body:

title: Strong winds interrupt crane operations across container terminal
author: Ellis Corven
body:

title: Berth Four repairs begin with reduced working area
author: Nina Halden
body:
Repair work began at Berth Four today after an inspection found worn fittings along the outer quay edge. A 95-metre section has been fenced off while crews replace six mooring bollards and repair the concrete around their foundations. The remaining 210 metres of the berth remain available for smaller vessels.

The authority has allocated KRN 8.4 million to the repairs, including replacement fenders and electrical checks. Two container services normally handled at Berth Four have been assigned to Berth Two. Shipping agents received revised working arrangements this morning, and the published berth list reflects those changes.

A marked pedestrian route runs behind the work area. Port users must keep clear of the fencing and follow instructions from quay staff. The inspection found no damage to the main quay structure. Cargo handling continues elsewhere in the terminal, with no change to freight gate opening hours.

title: North freight gate reopens after overnight equipment fault
author: Ellis Corven
body:
The north freight gate at the Port of Kestrel Bay reopened at 09:20 today after a fault in its vehicle recognition equipment. The gate closed at 02:15. Freight traffic used the south entrance while technicians replaced a damaged power unit and checked the control system.

A total of 186 lorry bookings were affected. Drivers with valid bookings were admitted through the south gate without making a second booking, and the authority waived missed-slot charges linked to the closure. The longest recorded queue was 38 vehicles shortly before 07:00. No injuries or damage to cargo were reported.

Both freight entrances are now operating normally. Drivers whose booking records still show a missed visit can ask the gate office to correct the entry, quoting their vehicle registration and booking number. The fault did not affect rail movements, vessel operations or access to the empty-container yard.

title: Container volumes rise as inland rail services expand
author: Mara Venn
body:

Rail carried 28 per cent of containers leaving the port by land, up from 24 per cent a year earlier. Two additional weekly services between the port and Amberford began operating in June. The inland terminal at Amberford now receives eight port trains each week.

Average lorry turnaround time was 43 minutes during July, measured from entry at the freight gate to departure. This was four minutes shorter than in June. The authority publishes these figures to help hauliers and cargo owners compare port performance. Empty containers and loaded containers are included in the gate measure.

author: Nina Halden
body:

title: Rail signalling fault delays inland container departures today
author: Ellis Corven
body:

One train was bound for Amberford and two for the Saltmarsh inland terminal. The line reopened at 13:40 following replacement of the faulty component and a test movement. The first delayed train left the port at 14:05. No containers were transferred to road transport during the closure.

Rail customers received revised departure details through their booking contacts. Containers held on the affected trains have been exempted from additional port storage charges caused by the interruption. Vessel loading and unloading continued throughout the incident, and freight gates remained open. The fault occurred outside the port boundary and did not affect the terminal's internal rail equipment.

title: Port clears delayed vessel queue after fog restrictions
author: Ellis Corven
body:
The Port of Kestrel Bay cleared its delayed vessel queue at 15:30 today after dense fog restricted harbour movements overnight. Visibility at the outer entrance fell below 200 metres, and vessel movements were suspended from 23:10 yesterday until 07:45 today. Five arriving vessels were held at the designated anchorage.

Harbour staff resumed movements after visibility improved and patrol crews checked the entrance channel. Departing vessels moved first where this released an occupied berth. Two container vessels, two general cargo ships and one coastal tanker then entered under revised arrival slots agreed with their agents.

Cargo work continued on vessels already alongside during the restriction. Freight gates and rail services operated normally, although collection times changed for some containers aboard the delayed arrivals. Customers can check release status through their usual account record. No collisions, groundings or injuries were reported during the fog restriction or the clearance of the queue.

title: New bilingual freight guidance supports Val-Brume cargo customers
author: Tomas Bellwick
body:
The Port of Kestrel Bay has published freight collection guidance in English and French following requests from cargo customers in Val-Brume. The guidance covers gate bookings, container release checks, driver identification and the documents needed to collect goods through an appointed haulier.

Customers with billing addresses in the French-speaking region accounted for 12 per cent of loaded import collections during the first nine months of this year. The port's customer team reviewed 160 enquiries from those customers when preparing the guidance. Missing release references and uncertainty about collection authority were the most common problems.

Both language versions are available from the freight desk and in the customer account area. Printed copies carry the same numbered steps so staff and drivers can refer to the same instruction. The guidance explains existing procedures and introduces no additional documents or charges. Customers can request help from a French-speaking member of the customer team.

title: Ostara workshop helps manufacturers check labels before printing
author: Elise Marvaux
body:
Thirty-four staff from 22 food businesses attended a label checking workshop in Ostara, organised by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. The session focused on common errors that can be caught before packaging goes to print.

Participants worked through fictional product labels covering soups, baked goods and chilled meals. Exercises included checking ingredient order, matching declared weights to product specifications and making storage instructions easy to find.

Elise Marvaux, technical affairs manager, said: “A second check against the recipe and specification can prevent an expensive reprint. Staff need a clear process for recording who approved a label and which version was sent to the printer.”

The federation distributed a two-page checklist and a sample approval record. The materials reflect current requirements and identify matters still under consultation in the draft labelling guidance. French versions are available to members through the federation’s advice service in Val-Brume.

title: Packaging levy revision removes duplicate reporting for manufacturers
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has welcomed a revised packaging levy proposal published today by the Ministry of Revenue. The revision provides for one reporting return and removes a provision that could have counted some packaging twice.

The proposed rate remains KRN 0.18 per kilogram for the materials covered. The ministry has also added examples showing how manufacturers should record packaging purchased through wholesalers and packaging transferred between factories.

Mara Vennick, policy director, said: “These changes address a practical problem raised in our submission. Businesses can now assess the proposal with a clearer understanding of what they would need to report.”

The federation continues to seek clarification on reusable transport containers and the treatment of returned goods. It has asked members to submit examples with weights and purchase records. The levy remains a proposal, and the federation advises businesses to distinguish the draft requirements from their existing reporting duties.

title: Wage talks open with focus on pay and training
author: Devran Pell
body:
Negotiations on Kestria’s next food manufacturing sector wage agreement opened in Saltmarsh today. The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria is representing 63 employers covered by the agreement, alongside representatives of the Food Production Workers Union.

The opening meeting covered basic pay, shift allowances and access to paid training. The current agreement provides a minimum hourly rate of KRN 14.20 for adult production workers at participating businesses.

Devran Pell, employment relations manager, said: “We want an agreement that improves pay and helps factories retain skilled people. Employers also need to understand the full cost, including allowances, before they can make a firm commitment.”

Both negotiating teams exchanged evidence on vacancies, staff turnover and business costs. No pay settlement was reached at the opening meeting. The federation has asked participating employers to check their payroll information so that further discussions use consistent figures for hours, grades and shift patterns.

title: New labelling guidance needs clearer examples for small producers
author: Elise Marvaux
body:
The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has asked the Food Standards Office to expand its draft guidance on ingredient labelling. Members say the document leaves uncertainty about how to display ingredients used within prepared fillings and sauces.

The federation reviewed 42 sample labels supplied by 18 manufacturers. Its technical team identified three recurring questions: where to place ingredient brackets, how to describe mixed oils and when a change in recipe requires revised packaging.

Elise Marvaux, technical affairs manager, said: “A bakery in Val-Brume should be able to reach the same answer as a sauce maker in Ostara. Clear examples would reduce mistakes and unnecessary calls for advice.”

The federation has submitted six worked examples and requested guidance in both Kestrian and French. It also recommends allowing businesses to use existing compliant packaging stocks when the change concerns presentation alone, provided all required consumer information remains accurate and legible.

title: Summer survey shows steady orders but tighter margins
author: Tomas Bellan
body:
Food manufacturers reported steady summer orders but continued pressure on margins, according to a survey published today by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. The survey received responses from 84 businesses employing 12,600 people.

Forty-six per cent said their order volumes were broadly unchanged from the previous three months. Thirty-one per cent reported an increase and 23 per cent a decline. Responses were collected between 10 and 24 August.

Packaging and maintenance were the most frequently reported sources of higher costs. Fifty-eight per cent of respondents said their operating margin had narrowed, while 37 per cent had postponed at least one planned equipment purchase.

Tomas Bellan, research manager, said: “Stable orders are welcome, but they do not mean every business is comfortable. Manufacturers in Amberford and Kestrel Bay described particular difficulty finding affordable replacement parts.” The federation cautioned that the voluntary survey represents participating members rather than the entire sector.

title: Manufacturers seek simpler rules for proposed packaging levy
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has called for changes to a proposed packaging levy, saying the current draft would require manufacturers to report the same material more than once.

In its submission to the Ministry of Revenue, the federation supports charging by packaging weight but asks for a single reporting return. The proposal sets a rate of KRN 0.18 per kilogram for certain packaging materials.

A review of records from 26 member businesses found that 19 would need to change their stock systems under the draft rules. Smaller manufacturers estimated an average initial cost of KRN 8,400, excluding staff time.

Mara Vennick, the federation’s policy director, said: “Members need clear definitions and a practical way to submit figures. One return, with worked examples, would help businesses meet the rules and make the information easier to check.”

title: Maintenance vacancies remain hardest to fill in autumn survey
author: Tomas Bellan
body:
Maintenance roles remain the hardest vacancies for food manufacturers to fill, according to a staffing survey released today by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. Seventy-six member businesses responded between 22 September and 2 October.

Among the 49 respondents recruiting during that period, 29 reported difficulty hiring maintenance staff. Twenty-one reported difficulty recruiting machine operators. Businesses could select more than one role, so the figures do not represent separate groups of employers.

Tomas Bellan, research manager, said: “Employers described a shortage of applicants with experience of fault finding and routine equipment care. Several businesses in Kestrel Bay said vacancies had increased their reliance on external repair services.”

Thirty-two respondents said they had increased internal training during the previous six months. The federation is using the findings in discussions with training providers in Amberford and Ostara. The survey did not measure the effect of the proposed wage settlement announced this week.

title: Employers and union reach proposed sector wage settlement
author: Devran Pell
body:
The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria and the Food Production Workers Union have reached a proposed sector wage settlement following negotiations in Saltmarsh. The proposal is subject to approval by participating employers and union members.

title: Summer survey shows steady orders but tighter margins
author: Tomas Bellan
body:

title: Manufacturers seek simpler rules for proposed packaging levy
author: Mara Vennick
body:
The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has called for changes to a proposed packaging levy, saying the current draft would require manufacturers to report the same material more than once.

In its submission to the Ministry of Revenue, the federation supports charging by packaging weight but asks for a single reporting return. The proposal sets a rate of KRN 0.18 per kilogram for certain packaging materials.

A review of records from 26 member businesses found that 19 would need to change their stock systems under the draft rules. Smaller manufacturers estimated an average initial cost of KRN 8,400, excluding staff time.

Mara Vennick, the federation’s policy director, said: “Members need clear definitions and a practical way to submit figures. One return, with worked examples, would help businesses meet the rules and make the information easier to check.”

title: Federation publishes costing guide for proposed wage agreement
author: Devran Pell
body:
The Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria has published a costing guide to help participating employers assess the proposed sector wage agreement. The guide accompanies the settlement terms circulated on 7 October.

Worked examples cover basic pay, shift allowances and paid training time. For an employee working 38 paid hours a week at the adult production minimum, the proposed hourly increase of KRN 0.65 would add KRN 24.70 to weekly basic pay.

The guide explains that this figure excludes overtime, allowances and employer contributions. It also asks businesses to account for training cover where production duties need to be reassigned during an employee’s eight annual paid training hours.

Devran Pell, employment relations manager, said: “Employers need to assess the whole agreement using their own staffing patterns. These examples provide a common starting point.” The proposal remains subject to approval, and the guide does not replace the full settlement document or individual employment contracts.

title: Maintenance vacancies remain hardest to fill in autumn survey
author: Tomas Bellan
body:
Maintenance roles remain the hardest vacancies for food manufacturers to fill, according to a staffing survey released today by the Food Manufacturers Federation of Kestria. Seventy-six member businesses responded between 22 September and 2 October.

Among the 49 respondents recruiting during that period, 29 reported difficulty hiring maintenance staff. Twenty-one reported difficulty recruiting machine operators. Businesses could select more than one role, so the figures do not represent separate groups of employers.

Tomas Bellan, research manager, said: “Employers described a shortage of applicants with experience of fault finding and routine equipment care. Several businesses in Kestrel Bay said vacancies had increased their reliance on external repair services.”

Thirty-two respondents said they had increased internal training during the previous six months. The federation is using the findings in discussions with training providers in Amberford and Ostara. The survey did not measure the effect of the proposed wage settlement announced this week.

title: Exchange extends afternoon trading for all agricultural futures
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange has extended its regular trading session by 30 minutes. From today, wheat, oat and rapeseed futures trade from 08:30 to 16:30, using the exchange clock in Ostara. The opening time is unchanged. Members can enter orders during the pre-opening period from 08:15.

The daily settlement calculation now uses eligible trading activity between 16:20 and 16:30. Where activity is insufficient, the exchange applies its existing rules for assessing bids, offers and related contract months. The longer session responds to requests from members handling afternoon warehouse confirmations in Amberford and freight arrangements through Kestrel Bay.

Orders marked to expire at the end of the trading day now remain active until 16:30 unless cancelled or filled. Orders carrying a specific expiry time retain that instruction. Members should review automated schedules and staffing arrangements. The extension does not alter delivery notice deadlines, collateral payment deadlines or the opening hours of approved warehouses.

title: Amberford warehouse approved for additional wheat delivery capacity
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange has approved a further 12,000 tonnes of wheat storage at the Merebank warehouse in Amberford. The additional capacity is eligible for exchange delivery from today. Approval follows checks of weighing equipment, sampling facilities, stock records and the separation of grain held for different owners.

The extension brings Merebank's approved wheat capacity to 30,000 tonnes. It does not add oat or rapeseed storage to the site's approval. Wheat placed into exchange delivery must meet the existing contract standards, including a maximum moisture content of 14.5 per cent. Warehouse approval does not replace the inspection required for each delivery lot.

Members arranging delivery should confirm available space directly with the warehouse before submitting a notice. The exchange's register now shows the additional capacity and the site's receiving hours. Merebank must report eligible stocks each trading day and notify the exchange immediately if equipment faults, access restrictions or stock discrepancies affect its ability to receive or release grain.

title: August trading figures show stronger activity in wheat futures
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange recorded 48,620 futures contracts traded in August, up from 44,180 in July. Wheat accounted for 27,340 contracts, oats for 8,760 and rapeseed for 12,520. The figures count each matched contract once and exclude orders that were cancelled or remained unfilled.

Wheat trading increased by 14 per cent compared with July, with the largest share of activity in the nearest two delivery months. Across all three commodities, open interest stood at 18,460 contracts at the August close. Open interest measures contracts that remain outstanding rather than the number traded during the month.

There were 286 completed delivery transfers during August, representing 5,720 tonnes. Approved warehouses in Amberford handled 124 transfers, Ostara handled 98 and Kestrel Bay handled 64. The monthly statistics file includes delivery totals and activity by contract month. Members can download it from the exchange's document service without a separate subscription charge.

title: Oat futures gain smaller price steps across listed months
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange has reduced the minimum price movement for oat futures from KRN 0.50 to KRN 0.25 per tonne. The change took effect at today's opening and applies to all listed delivery months. With a contract size of 20 tonnes, each minimum movement is now worth KRN 5.

The exchange introduced the smaller step after members requested more precise pricing between bids and offers. Orders entered before the change remain valid because prices quoted in half-crown increments also meet the new quarter-crown requirement. Contract quantities, delivery standards and the method used to calculate daily settlement prices have not changed.

Members should check that their order systems accept prices ending in .25 and .75, as well as .00 and .50. The exchange's test service includes sample orders using each permitted ending. Support staff in Ostara and Val-Brume are handling queries about rejected prices and the display of contract values on member screens.

title: Rapeseed margins increased following wider daily price movements
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange has increased the initial margin on rapeseed futures to KRN 2,400 per contract, from KRN 2,100. The maintenance margin rises to KRN 2,000, from KRN 1,750. The revised requirements apply to positions held at today's clearing calculation and cover every listed rapeseed delivery month.

The change follows a review of price movements over the past ten trading sessions. The average daily price range reached KRN 21 per tonne, compared with KRN 14 during the preceding review period. Each rapeseed contract represents 20 tonnes. Margin is collateral against potential losses and is separate from the contract's purchase price.

Clearing members must meet any resulting collateral shortfall by 09:00 on the next trading day. Eligible collateral and payment instructions are unchanged. Wheat and oat margin requirements remain at their existing levels. The exchange reviews margins each trading day and can adjust them when price movements or the concentration of positions warrant a change.

title: Exchange publishes revised delivery guide for grain futures
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange has published a revised delivery guide for its wheat and oat futures. The guide brings warehouse instructions, sampling rules and delivery forms into one document. It applies to delivery notices submitted from today and does not change the quantity represented by either contract.

Both contracts cover 20 tonnes. Approved delivery locations remain Ostara, Amberford and Kestrel Bay. Sellers must identify the warehouse, stored quantity and inspection reference on each notice. Buyers can request a second sample where the first inspection records a result within 0.2 percentage points of a contract quality limit.

The guide also explains how warehouse charges are divided when ownership changes. Storage remains the seller's responsibility through the transfer date, with the buyer responsible from the following day. Members can obtain the guide through the exchange's document service. A French-language version is available for members and warehouse operators in Val-Brume.

title: Trading resumes after morning interruption to order entry
body:
Trading in wheat, oat and rapeseed futures resumed at 10:05 today after an interruption to the exchange's order entry service. Ostara Commodities Exchange suspended matching at 09:12 when monitoring identified delays in order acknowledgements. A ten-minute period for members to review and cancel orders preceded the reopening.

Trades completed before the suspension remain valid. Orders that had been accepted and remained unfilled were retained with their original priority. Messages that did not receive an acceptance acknowledgement were not added to the order book. Members were asked to reconcile their records against the exchange's order and trade reports before entering replacement instructions.

Technical staff traced the interruption to a fault in a message queue and moved the service to reserve equipment. The regular 16:30 closing time remains in place. Clearing and warehouse reporting services continued to operate during the interruption. The exchange is reviewing system records and member reports to establish why the fault was not resolved automatically.

title: September statistics record higher open interest across agricultural contracts
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange recorded open interest of 20,180 contracts at the September close, an increase of 1,720 from August. Wheat accounted for 11,420 outstanding contracts, oats for 3,160 and rapeseed for 5,600. All three products ended September with more outstanding contracts than at the previous month end.

September trading volume totalled 51,260 contracts. This comprised 29,100 wheat contracts, 9,040 oat contracts and 13,120 rapeseed contracts. The busiest session recorded 3,480 contracts across the exchange. Volume counts completed trades during the month, while open interest records positions that remained outstanding after clearing at the month end.

Approved warehouses completed 312 delivery transfers, equivalent to 6,240 tonnes. Of these, 174 transfers were wheat, 58 were oats and 80 were rapeseed. The full statistics file is available through the exchange's document service. It includes daily trading totals and a breakdown by delivery month, with explanatory notes on how cancelled trades are treated.

title: Wheat margin requirements rise after increased market volatility
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange has raised the initial margin for wheat futures from KRN 1,600 to KRN 1,900 per contract. The maintenance margin increases from KRN 1,300 to KRN 1,550. The new requirements apply to all listed wheat months at today's clearing calculation, including positions opened before the announcement.

The adjustment reflects larger daily price movements and a greater concentration of positions in the nearest delivery month. Over the past five sessions, the average wheat price range was KRN 17 per tonne. Each contract covers 20 tonnes. The exchange has made no change to wheat delivery specifications or permitted price increments.

Clearing members must provide any additional collateral by 09:00 on the next trading day. Members may apply higher requirements to their own clients under their account agreements. Oat and rapeseed margins are unchanged by this notice. The exchange continues to assess both price risk and the time needed to close positions when setting its collateral requirements.

title: Rapeseed delivery rules clarify sampling and retained records
body:

title: Trading resumes after morning interruption to order entry
body:
Trading in wheat, oat and rapeseed futures resumed at 10:05 today after an interruption to the exchange's order entry service. Ostara Commodities Exchange suspended matching at 09:12 when monitoring identified delays in order acknowledgements. A ten-minute period for members to review and cancel orders preceded the reopening.

Trades completed before the suspension remain valid. Orders that had been accepted and remained unfilled were retained with their original priority. Messages that did not receive an acceptance acknowledgement were not added to the order book. Members were asked to reconcile their records against the exchange's order and trade reports before entering replacement instructions.

Clearing and warehouse reporting services continued to operate during the interruption. The exchange is reviewing system records and member reports to establish why the fault was not resolved automatically.

title: September statistics record higher open interest across agricultural contracts
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange recorded open interest of 20,180 contracts at the September close, an increase of 1,720 from August. Wheat accounted for 11,420 outstanding contracts, oats for 3,160 and rapeseed for 5,600. All three products ended September with more outstanding contracts than at the previous month end.

September trading volume totalled 51,260 contracts. This comprised 29,100 wheat contracts, 9,040 oat contracts and 13,120 rapeseed contracts. The busiest session recorded 3,480 contracts across the exchange. Volume counts completed trades during the month, while open interest records positions that remained outstanding after clearing at the month end.

Approved warehouses completed 312 delivery transfers, equivalent to 6,240 tonnes. Of these, 174 transfers were wheat, 58 were oats and 80 were rapeseed. The full statistics file is available through the exchange's document service. It includes daily trading totals and a breakdown by delivery month, with explanatory notes on how cancelled trades are treated.

title: Wheat margin requirements rise after increased market volatility
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange has raised the initial margin for wheat futures from KRN 1,600 to KRN 1,900 per contract. The maintenance margin increases from KRN 1,300 to KRN 1,550. The new requirements apply to all listed wheat months at today's clearing calculation, including positions opened before the announcement.

The adjustment reflects larger daily price movements and a greater concentration of positions in the nearest delivery month. Over the past five sessions, the average wheat price range was KRN 17 per tonne. Each contract covers 20 tonnes. The exchange has made no change to wheat delivery specifications or permitted price increments.

Oat and rapeseed margins are unchanged by this notice. The exchange continues to assess both price risk and the time needed to close positions when setting its collateral requirements.

title: Exchange extends afternoon trading for all agricultural futures
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange has extended its regular trading session by 30 minutes. From today, wheat, oat and rapeseed futures trade from 08:30 to 16:30, using the exchange clock in Ostara. The opening time is unchanged. Members can enter orders during the pre-opening period from 08:15.

The daily settlement calculation now uses eligible trading activity between 16:20 and 16:30. Where activity is insufficient, the exchange applies its existing rules for assessing bids, offers and related contract months. The longer session responds to requests from members handling afternoon warehouse confirmations in Amberford and freight arrangements through Kestrel Bay.

Orders marked to expire at the end of the trading day now remain active until 16:30 unless cancelled or filled. Orders carrying a specific expiry time retain that instruction. Members should review automated schedules and staffing arrangements. The extension does not alter delivery notice deadlines, collateral payment deadlines or the opening hours of approved warehouses.

title: Amberford warehouse approved for additional wheat delivery capacity
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange has approved a further 12,000 tonnes of wheat storage at the Merebank warehouse in Amberford. The additional capacity is eligible for exchange delivery from today. Approval follows checks of weighing equipment, sampling facilities, stock records and the separation of grain held for different owners.

The extension brings Merebank's approved wheat capacity to 30,000 tonnes. It does not add oat or rapeseed storage to the site's approval. Wheat placed into exchange delivery must meet the existing contract standards, including a maximum moisture content of 14.5 per cent. Warehouse approval does not replace the inspection required for each delivery lot.

Members arranging delivery should confirm available space directly with the warehouse before submitting a notice. The exchange's register now shows the additional capacity and the site's receiving hours. Merebank must report eligible stocks each trading day and notify the exchange immediately if equipment faults, access restrictions or stock discrepancies affect its ability to receive or release grain.

title: August trading figures show stronger activity in wheat futures
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange recorded 48,620 futures contracts traded in August, up from 44,180 in July. Wheat accounted for 27,340 contracts, oats for 8,760 and rapeseed for 12,520. The figures count each matched contract once and exclude orders that were cancelled or remained unfilled.

Wheat trading increased by 14 per cent compared with July, with the largest share of activity in the nearest two delivery months. Across all three commodities, open interest stood at 18,460 contracts at the August close. Open interest measures contracts that remain outstanding rather than the number traded during the month.

There were 286 completed delivery transfers during August, representing 5,720 tonnes. Approved warehouses in Amberford handled 124 transfers, Ostara handled 98 and Kestrel Bay handled 64. The monthly statistics file includes delivery totals and activity by contract month. Members can download it from the exchange's document service without a separate subscription charge.

title: Exchange introduces calendar spread orders for wheat futures
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange has introduced calendar spread orders for wheat futures. Members can now submit a single order to buy one listed wheat delivery month and sell another in equal quantities. The service is available during the regular 08:30 to 16:30 session and uses the same contract specifications as outright wheat trading.

Spread prices represent the price of the later delivery month minus the price of the earlier month, quoted in KRN per tonne. The minimum price movement is KRN 0.25 per tonne, equivalent to KRN 5 for a spread covering one 20-tonne contract in each month. Both sides execute together, removing the need to submit two separate outright orders.

Completed spreads create a separate futures position in each delivery month. Existing delivery obligations and position limits continue to apply to those positions. The exchange's published margin schedule determines the collateral required, including any eligible offset between months. Members can access worked examples and test messages through the document and test services. Oat and rapeseed order types are unchanged.

title: Rapeseed margins reduced as daily price ranges narrow
body:
Ostara Commodities Exchange has reduced the initial margin on rapeseed futures from KRN 2,400 to KRN 2,200 per contract. The maintenance margin falls from KRN 2,000 to KRN 1,850. The revised requirements apply at today's clearing calculation across all listed rapeseed delivery months, with no change to contract size.

The reduction follows a sustained narrowing of daily price ranges. The average range over the latest ten trading sessions was KRN 15 per tonne, compared with KRN 21 at the August review that led to higher margins. The exchange also assessed outstanding positions and the volume available to close them during normal trading.

Any collateral made available by the reduction remains subject to the member's other obligations and the exchange's normal withdrawal checks. The lower requirement does not change the daily settlement of gains and losses. Wheat initial margin remains KRN 1,900 per contract. Oat requirements are unchanged. Members should consult their clearing statements for the effect on individual accounts.

title: Annual report records faster action on unpaid pension contributions
author: Mara Ellwick
body:
The Pensions Oversight Authority's annual report, published today, records KRN 6.8 million in overdue employer contributions recovered following its intervention during the year ended 31 March 2026. The payments reached 73 workplace pension plans covering 18,420 members. Recoveries totalled KRN 5.1 million in the previous reporting year.

The median time from opening a contribution case to securing payment fell from 47 to 34 working days. The Authority issued 29 financial penalties and required improvements to record keeping at 61 plans. These figures cover completed cases; they do not include money still being pursued at the year end.

Operating expenditure was KRN 24.6 million against a budget of KRN 25.2 million. The report includes audited accounts, service measures and a breakdown of complaints about the Authority. Priorities for the current year include earlier checks on missed payments and clearer guidance for employers running smaller workplace plans.

title: Val-Brume pension clinic offers support with annual returns
author: Celia Bramwell
body:
Trustees and employers in the Val-Brume area can now book free appointments at a pension reporting clinic on 8 October. Staff from the Pensions Oversight Authority will explain common annual return requirements and help visitors identify information missing from their records. Appointments will be available in French and English.

The clinic will take place at the Authority's Val-Brume office, with 36 appointments lasting 25 minutes each. Visitors should bring their plan registration number and a list of questions. They should not bring members' identity documents, bank details or individual medical records. Telephone appointments are available for those unable to attend.

The service follows a review of 94 returns from plans administered in the region. The most frequent errors concerned membership totals and changes to trustee contact details. Staff can explain reporting requirements but cannot complete returns for applicants or provide investment advice. Booking closes on 5 October, unless all appointments are filled earlier.

title: Consultation opens on clearer recovery plans for underfunded pensions
author: Tomas Vennick
body:
The Pensions Oversight Authority is seeking views on proposed changes to the information employers and trustees provide when a workplace pension plan is underfunded. The consultation opens today and closes on 30 October. The proposals concern plans that promise members a set retirement income.

Under the proposals, recovery plans would explain why the payment schedule is affordable, what would happen if trading weakened and how trustees would monitor progress. A standard summary would show annual contributions in KRN alongside the expected funding shortfall. The Authority is also asking whether smaller plans need a shorter reporting form.

No funding rules change today. Existing recovery plans and payment schedules remain in force. Employers, trustees, advisers and members can respond through the Authority's consultation service or by post to its Saltmarsh office. An accompanying paper includes worked examples for a manufacturer, a transport business and a community services employer.

title: Amberford employer fined after repeated delays to pension contributions
author: Leila Corven
body:
The Pensions Oversight Authority has fined Amberford employer Brindle Quay Components KRN 42,000 after it repeatedly paid workplace pension contributions late. The company missed payment deadlines in seven months between September 2025 and April 2026. The delays affected 286 members of its workplace pension plan.

The employer has now paid the outstanding KRN 193,400, together with KRN 8,760 to compensate the plan for lost investment income. The fine is separate from those payments and must be paid by the company. It cannot be taken from pension assets or charged to members.

The Authority issued its final decision after considering the company's response to an earlier notice. The company has 28 days to appeal. Trustees have been asked to check contributions each month and report further delays. Members do not need to submit individual claims to receive the compensation within the plan.

title: Employers given clearer steps for reporting late pension payments
author: Tomas Vennick
body:
The Pensions Oversight Authority has published guidance explaining how employers and trustees should report late workplace pension contributions. It includes examples covering payroll errors, missing payment references and repeated delays. The guidance applies to reports made from today and does not change the legal payment deadlines.

Trustees should record when a payment was due, the amount outstanding and the steps taken to recover it. Where a report is required, it should distinguish money deducted from staff pay from contributions owed by the employer. Employers should give trustees a named contact who can resolve payment queries.

During the first six months of 2026, the Authority received 318 reports involving late payments. Of these, 241 were resolved within 20 working days of the initial report. The new guidance includes a reporting checklist and sample payment record, with versions available in English and French.

title: Workplace pension funding improves in second quarter review
author: Mara Ellwick
body:
The Pensions Oversight Authority estimates that workplace pension plans promising a set retirement income held assets equal to 104 per cent of their liabilities at the end of June. This compares with 102 per cent at the end of March. The review covers 842 plans across Kestria, with combined assets of KRN 186 billion.

The improvement mainly reflects higher investment income and employer contributions. Funding remains uneven: 176 plans held less than the estimated amount needed to meet their promises. A national average does not show whether an individual plan can pay every benefit when it falls due.

Employers and trustees should continue making scheduled payments and reviewing their funding assumptions. The figures are estimates based on quarterly returns, rather than full valuations of every plan. The Authority has published regional tables, including separate results for Saltmarsh, Kestrel Bay, Ostara, Amberford and Val-Brume.

title: Kestrel Bay trustees directed to replace incomplete pension records
author: Leila Corven
body:
The Pensions Oversight Authority has directed the trustees of the Merehaven Packaging Retirement Plan in Kestrel Bay to repair incomplete membership records. An inspection found missing service dates or pay histories for 417 of the plan's 2,860 members. These records are needed to calculate promised retirement benefits accurately.

The trustees must produce a costed repair programme within 30 days and complete the work by 31 March 2027. They must also arrange an independent check of corrected records and send monthly progress reports to the Authority. The direction follows an earlier request for improvements that was not completed.

The inspection did not find evidence that assets were missing. Existing pension payments will continue, and the administrator will contact members if it needs information from them. Members should retain old benefit statements and employment records where available. The trustees have 28 days to appeal against the direction.

title: Trustees asked to check member addresses before annual statements
author: Celia Bramwell
body:
The Pensions Oversight Authority is asking workplace pension trustees to check their member contact records before issuing annual benefit statements this autumn. A review of 120 plans found that 8.4 per cent of statements sent during the previous reporting cycle were returned or could not be delivered electronically.

Plans should compare their records with recent updates from members and employers, investigate returned post and provide a straightforward way to correct an address. Trustees should take particular care with former employees who still hold benefits in the plan. An employer's current payroll list will not necessarily include these members.

The Authority has published a short checklist covering address checks, secure identity verification and records of delivery failures. Members who have moved should contact their pension administrator using details from an existing statement. They should never be asked to pay a fee simply to update their postal or email address.

title: Val-Brume clinic identifies common questions about pension membership totals
author: Celia Bramwell
body:
The Pensions Oversight Authority has published additional annual return guidance following its reporting clinic in Val-Brume on 8 October. Staff held 34 appointments with employers and trustees, including nine by telephone. Most questions concerned how to count members who had left employment but retained pension benefits.

The updated guidance explains how to report contributing members, members with benefits left in a plan and members already receiving a pension. It also covers people who appear in more than one category during a reporting year. Worked examples show which position to record on the return's specified reporting date.

The examples are available in French and English and can be used by plans throughout Kestria. They clarify existing requirements and do not introduce new categories. Plans that have already submitted a return should check the guidance and contact the Authority if they identify a material error. Routine contact changes can be submitted through the usual update service.

title: New guidance explains pension duties when employers change payroll
author: Tomas Vennick
body:
Employers changing payroll systems should test pension deductions before the first live pay run, according to guidance published today by the Pensions Oversight Authority. The guidance addresses errors involving contribution rates, pensionable pay and the transfer of employee records. It applies to employers of all sizes.

The Authority reviewed 52 contribution incidents linked to payroll changes between January and August 2026. In 31 cases, an incorrect setting was copied across a whole group of employees. The guidance recommends checking sample calculations, agreeing payment references with the pension administrator and confirming who will investigate any mismatch.

Changing a payroll provider does not change an employer's responsibility to pay contributions in full and on time. Employers should keep a record of checks and explain corrections clearly to affected staff. The publication includes examples for weekly and monthly payrolls, together with a handover checklist that can be shared with payroll providers.

title: Third quarter figures show fewer unresolved pension payment reports
author: Mara Ellwick
body:
There were 64 unresolved reports of late workplace pension contributions at 30 September, down from 81 at 30 June, according to figures published today by the Pensions Oversight Authority. The figures count reports under investigation and do not represent every late payment across Kestria.

The Authority received 147 new reports during the third quarter and closed 164. Of the closed reports, 139 ended with full payment, 17 concerned reporting errors and eight were combined with existing investigations. Reports can cover several missed payments by the same employer, so case numbers should not be read as employer totals.

Among the unresolved reports, 12 had been open for more than 90 days. These included disputed payroll records and employers experiencing financial difficulty. Trustees should continue pursuing unpaid contributions while an investigation is open. Reporting a delay to the Authority does not transfer responsibility for collecting payments from the plan's trustees.
